entry_admission_input_domain.entry: UtilityController registry maps JP 41/43/57 and NA 1041/1043/1057 to DCMService. Controller init stores initArgs.utilId, resolves current ecuId from commonInfo, constructs model/initial view/dialog/CommonInfo, initializes initial view and opens DL012.
entry_admission_input_domain.actual_switch: Controller switch recognizes only literal1041,1043,1057. Shell onClickNextBtn gets utilInfo by selected ID then calls nextController.init(utilInfo) unchanged; worker row id becomes utilId directly. Registered JP41/43/57 are therefore delivered unchanged and execute no case/default: initial view and DL012 stay open, no worker initializer called. Evidence composed with MenuShell utility_controller.js.onClickNextBtn and utility_worker getUtilInfoByUtilId.
entry_admission_input_domain.selection: Select view selectedService starts -1; Next disabled until Activate DCM radio sets 0 or ACN call end radio sets 1; event emits selectedService,utilId. Controller reads evt.args[1] and evt.args[2].
entry_admission_input_domain.ecu_domain: Worker resolves commonInfo.getEcuInfoByEcuId(ecuId).busId and for DTC also phaseType. No phase-specific frontend path. userType.filePath, userInfo.userId, networkStatus, CID strings and PF replies remain typed runtime inputs.

state_fields.view: Select selectedService/utilId and cached jQuery controls; timer count interval handle. Other views own event dispatcher and panes. Constructors unused modeA8Size/webRcvData/countdown do not imply timers or requests.

send rejection sets sendMessageError; other rejection copies resultInfo.detailCode. All failures set isCommonError; if endFlg, attempts SC14 and swallows its failure. Controller send error shows communication dialog then menu; other error uses common error dialog then menu.

Success controller stores networkStatus, logs DCM Service title, closes DL012, disposes initial view, shows select view and registers Next/Exit.
Failure copies resultInfo.detailCode and isCommonError:true; if endFlg attempts SC14 swallowing cleanup error; returns result, not a worker rejection. Controller common error dialog OK returns menu.

initCache; SC13 {ecuId,busId}, sets endFlg=true only on success; UG17 {opt:1}, UG17 {opt:3}, UG19 {ecuId,busId,opt:1,id:0x25,bytePos:0,bitPos:[0xFF repeated 15]}, UG20 {ecuId,busId,opt:3,id:0x2E} -> size2E; SC14 {}.

Success logs title and opens select view, without controller networkStatus assignment. Error sets isCommonError/detailCode, attempts SC14 iff endFlg and swallows cleanup failure; controller common error OK returns menu.
Always logs resource r_item_i1957 concatenated with selected radio label; retained data radio label.

DCM01/04 activation requires controller.networkStatus===1; if not, DL001 network warning OK merely closes dialog, keeping selection. If online, dispose select and show GetCid view (Back->selection,Next->getCID,Exit->exit confirmation).

DCM01/04 ACN opens ACNExe01. DCM17 activation opens DCMExe17 and ACN opens ACNExe17; Back->selection, Exit->confirmation. These three execution views declare BEXT_BTN but register/emit NEXT_BTN (undefined). Composed shell.EventDispatcher uses plain-object key coercion and CustomEvent string coercion, so matching undefined registration+trigger DELIVERS callbacks. Dispatcher does not await callback promises.

DL012; worker resets all three CID cache fields; DV83 {ecuId}; rejects absent/empty cidList, iterates list and assigns matching DCM1/2/3 data. DCM1 first char code !=0x31 -> isMEID:true. Requires all three fields !==undefined; no explicit empty-string validation.

Success closes DL012. isMEID true launches onClickNEXTBTN03 directly with no return of inner promise; else opens 10sec timer screen. Worker catch returns isCommonError/detailCode; controller common error OK returns selection.
Timer screen Next->webServiceExecute, Back->GetCid, Exit->special exit confirmation. Timer expires by clicking Back, not by activating service.

DL002; DV90 {} -> cache.vin; IF3 {} -> cache.packageVer; five serial IF12 reads from userType.filePath (health URL,activation URL,domainType,health ID,activation ID); UP5 {userId}, JSON.parse userProfile -> body.language.code; DV8 DTC request; nonempty dtcList -> DL004 and reject before web.

POST health request; sets dispDlgCode=8 before PF; parse responseData JSON; commonResult.statusCode MIR2000000 -> cache.isPrlUpdate=apiResult.isPrlUpdate; other with nonempty faultMessage -> DL005/faultMessage, else remains DL008; reject.
PUT activation request; status MIR2000000 -> cache MDN/MIN/SID; lengths must be 10/10/5 else DL001 and reject; isPrlUpdate truthy -> DL006 and reject; otherwise dispDlgCode=0 and continue.

SC13 {ecuId,busId} sets startFlg=true on success; four ordered UG15 writes 3B01,3B05,3B09,3B02; success resolves with communication STILL OPEN. This open session is intentionally continued in matchECU after user ignition instructions; no success-path SC14 here.

On catch while dispDlgCode===0: set isCommonError, copy detailCode unless sendMessageError. Independently if startFlg, SC14 attempted and its failure swallowed. Nonzero dialog code suppresses commonError classification. All covered operational failures resolve result object, except malformed exception shapes can throw while accessing resultInfo.

Then query2129; (resBody[2]&3)===1 required else same mismatch; finally SC14, setting endFlg=false before call. Catch attempts SC14 iff endFlg and swallows cleanup error; only non-mismatch errors set isCommonError, copy detail unless send error.

Controller closes DL007. Common send error -> communication dialog then selection; other common error -> common error dialog then selection. dispDL008 shows Try Again/Exit dialog but does NOT return: it immediately also disposes current view and creates DCMResult01 success view. Try Again returns selection; Exit returns menu. This fallthrough is current source behavior.

Send errors classified sendMessageError/isCommonError; other errors detailCode/isCommonError. Controller error paths return selection via dialogs; success opens ignition-cycle ConnectionView, Next opens ACNResult01 without another PF call.

mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.semantics: Timer starts Date(now seconds+10) (new Date drops milliseconds), initial displayed floor(delta/1000)+1; each500ms recomputes delta, displays floor+1; <=0 clears interval and triggers Back button click, whose handler clears and emits BACK_BTN. Next/Exit click also clears interval. Exit No invokes countdownTimer anew (full10sec); Exit Yes returns menu. disposeView itself DOES NOT clear interval, so non-button disposal can leave it alive. No cancellation PF API in this workflow.

Exit normal shows DL009 Yes->backPreviousScreen; any other choice no transition; finally closes dialog. Timer Exit No restarts timer. Back01 returns selection; Back02 disposes current and recreates GetCid. backPreviousScreen only triggers BACK_TO_UTILITY_MENU and resolves; no worker cleanup there. Controller dispose only current view.disposeView then eventDisp.dispose and resolves, no SC14/timeout teardown. Successful Exit logs successful-utility text then emits menu event.

Explicit SC14 calls and guards are detailed in ordered transitions; legacy web success intentionally leaves connection alive until matchECU. Leaving connection instructions through shell disposal has no local fallback SC14. Each workflow cleanup handles only its own endFlg/startFlg; does not prove global native communication teardown. Activity report logForTitle/logForText attempts are real host reporting side effects.

unit_contracts.purpose: Configuration: save vehicle configuration before replacement; restore saved configuration or server as-built after replacement; calibration URL handoff for PCM/TCM; DTC-clear and upload/deferred upload of completion records.
business_sequence: init captures current ECU ID, clears controller saveAsbuilt, starts blank screen plus loader immediately (showDialog001 is invoked as .then argument, not a deferred callback), awaits worker init; init isError shows DL010 and exits on acknowledgment; otherwise screen01; finally always closes loader.

Screen01 Next -> screen02; Back -> screen01. Screen02 starts with selectedMode -1 and Next disabled; selecting Before=0 or After=1 enables Next. Before is disabled for TCM852. Before logs selection, captures Date, writeLogDataFile; isError -> DL003 acknowledgment stays; success -> screen03 showing VIN and locale date, logs success, OK -> screen02.

After PCM851 -> getUrlPcm; error DL008 acknowledgment stays, success opens url in _blank then screen04. Screen04 Next -> getAsbuiltData/XML parse/sendAsbuiltData; Exit -> DL002. After TCM852 -> getUrlTcm; success opens url _blank then screen05; screen05 Exit logs success and immediately disposes/emits back. Other ECUs perform retrieval/parse/write directly.

getAsbuiltData isError saves response timestamp and selects dialog by errorType. Successful XML is parsed; parse isError goes to mapped dialog; send result sets controller.saveAsbuilt even on failure. Success closes loader -> screen06. Restart Next awaits clearDtc but does not inspect isError -> screen07. Complete Exit logs success and saveAsbuiltProgram; isError -> DL010 Exit, otherwise dispose/back.

DL002 Yes: if controller.saveAsbuilt, saveAsbuiltProgram first and error DL010; else immediate dispose/back. No leaves view. DL004 displays saved VIN/time; Yes calls sendAsbuiltData with undefined asbuiltData (vehicle cache path), disposes modal; error -> DL005, success -> screen06. No -> dispose modal -> DL007 delete confirmation. DL007 Yes deletes .acnf, disposes modal; error DL010show002, else screen02 unless already there. No disposes modal and returns screen02 unless already there.

DL005 Yes only retries PCM getUrlPcm; success opens URL and screen04, error DL008 then screen02; non-PCM Yes resolves without retry. DL005 No calls saveAsbuiltProgram (extra arguments ignored by model), then error DL010 or dispose/back. DL006 acknowledgment exits. DL008/DL009 TryAgain merely resolve; no automatic retry. DL010Exit exits; DL010DeleteConfig acknowledgment shows loader, deletes .acnf without checking returned isError, hides loader, screen02; DL010show002 returns screen02.

Error mapping is confirmWriteback4->DL004, writeBackFails5->DL005, doesNotExist6->DL006, webServiceError8->DL008, offline9->DL009, fails10->DL010DeleteConfig. showHelp is an actual empty supplied implementation. View disposal empties panes/disposes dispatcher/hides title; custom modal disposal removes body modal-open/backdrop, hides #v_datalogger_manager, empties #modal_dialog and disposes dispatcher. Controller dispose does not call worker/session cleanup.

worker_semantics.initCnf01: Cache ecuId, commonInfo VIN, userType filePath, sFlag=false, saveAsbuilt=false. getSpecificFolder({folderNo:1}) takes folderInfoList[0].folderInfo; getSettingFileInfo({fileType:2,keyList:[specificSubFolders,utilityConfiguration]}) parsed STRING appends config directory. Enumerate *.scnf; listing rejection resolves empty. If records exist read saveAsbuiltProgram setting (OBJECT), serially await each readFile -> POST original file data -> JSON response commonResult.statusCode MIR2000000 -> deleteFile; POST failure for a record is swallowed and leaves file, while read/settings/delete failure marks final isError=true. No records avoids setting/POST.
worker_semantics.writeLogDataFile: startGeneralComm({ecuId,busId:18}) -> transitSession({modeId:3}) -> serial DID reads by reverse ECU name -> [19,02,0f] DTC check -> conditional transitSession1 -> conditional endGeneralComm -> writeFile({path:configPath+\+VIN+_+ecuId+.acnf,mode:1,data:JSON.stringify({vin,time:local YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss,did})}). DID sets: PCM f188,de00; IC de00,de01,f106; RCM de00,f190; SSU de00,de01; BCM de01. Response DID is bytes1,2 hex; data slice3, f188 drops zeros. DTC response length2 accepted, else stride4 starting3: first two bytes compared against a477,e100,9a84,f000,c300,0601,0602,0610 and matching rejects. mode03/generalComm flags set only on success, cleared before cleanup calls. Catch attempts conditional session1 then end and returns isError true; cleanup session1 rejection can escape that catch chain. Success returns false.
worker_semantics.getUrlPcm: List *.acnf, exact VIN_ecuId.acnf match; listing error means unavailable. Read userType getCalAtConfig OBJECT -> calibrationType OBJECT fileType1 and ecuId_<id>.mainTypeId decimal or null -> read matching .acnf JSON if available and cache did -> POST JSON {vin,cid:available?ASCII nonzero did.f188:null,cType}; MIR2000000 gets apiResult.cuwUrl. Any error -> {isError:true}; success includes url.
worker_semantics.getUrlTcm: Read getCalAtConfig and calibrationType as PCM; no .acnf lookup, POST {vin,cid:null,cType}; same status predicate/result.
worker_semantics.getAsbuiltData: List exact .acnf file. If present read and JSON parse to cache.readData, timestamp=readData.time, configSrc VEHICLE, deliberately reject to return isError true/errorType4 (confirmWriteback); read failure errorType10. If absent BCM -> errorType6; other ECUs get userType getAsbuiltData setting and POST contentType XML with <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><vin>VIN</vin>; successful response caches configSrc ASBUILT and returns responseData unparsed XML. Settings/web errors -> 8 or loginMode===2 ->9. Error result includes timestamp.
worker_semantics.sendAsbuiltData: Cache supplied asbuiltData; start general bus18 -> session3 -> requestSecurityAccess with PCM{level:0x43,logId:4}, IC/RCM/SSU/BCM{level:0x23,logId:5/6/7/8}. Serially await all 2e frames from exact source branch table. VEHICLE writes cached did payloads: PCM de00; IC de00,de01,f106; RCM de00,f190; SSU de00,de01; BCM de01. ASBUILT IC de00 seq1 and f106 seq2; RCM de00 value and f190 paddedVIN; SSU de00 value; PCM transformed VIN/filler/value slices exact ordered_body. Then set cache.saveAsbuilt=true BEFORE [11,01] reset request. Both success and failure attempt conditional session1 and end, swallowing both cleanup failures. Return isError,saveAsbuilt; failure errorType5. Earlier writes/reset may have occurred when result isError.
worker_semantics.clearDtc: Set sFlag=true BEFORE PF clearDtc({ecuId}); returns isError=false/true with rejection swallowed. Controller does not inspect flag.
worker_semantics.saveAsbuiltProgram: Construct {vin,vehicleConnectionId:vehicleInfo.getConfiguration?.apiResult?.vehicleConnectSession,ecuId:decimal string,ecuName,configSrc,sFlag:TRUE/FALSE}. If sFlag delete .acnf first (failure swallowed). Load saveAsbuiltProgram setting -> POST JSON requiring MIR2000000; POST/status failure falls back writeFile mode1 VIN_localYYYYMMDDhhmmss.scnf with identical request JSON. Settings/fallback file failure isError true; success including deferred file isError false. Does not require cache.saveAsbuilt.

unit_contracts.native_ownership: Frontend construction/order/predicate/cleanup only; PF/native implementation and actual ECU outcomes remain native owners.
unit_contracts.common_ui_contract: View init loads exact PAGE/gts_main_panel (custom Cnf modal IDs differ), sets localized title, appends panes, draws resources, binds exact DOM events and requests resize. Ordinary dispose empties owned panes/disposes event dispatcher/hides title; any exceptions, timers, table and resize-specific behavior are preserved in full method evidence. User events forward through EventDispatcher args into bound controller callbacks; no extra validation/cancellation/cleanup inferred.
unit_contracts.xml: DOMParser text/xml; statusCode missing becomes empty. Only MIR2000000 executes extraction, so nonmatching status can return success with empty arrays (actual source). asBuiltDataXml text replaces <,> then parses. VIN removes literal spaces and encodes UTF-16 charCodeAt; VALUE removes literal spaces and parses pairs hex. NAME exact matching, first DATA/VALUE; IC requires SEQ string1/2. PCM VIN17/value82; IC seq1=32 seq2=264; RCM VIN17/value12 then append seven zeros to VIN; SSU value13. No BCM extraction case. Invalid required lengths choose offline9 for loginMode2 else8.
unit_contracts.entry_admission: Registered JP/NA CNF_01 controller; current ECU captured on init. Supported ECU dispatch keys are PCM851,TCM852,IC853,RCM854,SSU855,BCM856; no added admission fallback for unknown ECU. Initial worker setup must return !isError before main screen.

input_domain.ui: Before0 or After1 radio; Before disabled for TCM852; Next disabled until selection; saved-file writeback/delete and exit Yes/No; acknowledgment and TryAgain buttons.
input_domain.vehicle: commonInfo VIN, selected ECU identity/name, loginMode, vehicleConnectSession and userType filePath.
input_domain.external: Configuration directory setting, *.acnf and *.scnf listings, matching VIN_ecuId.acnf JSON, server endpoint objects, calibrationType ECU entry, as-built XML, PF responses.
input_domain.transform: Saved VIN/time displayed; XML VIN removes spaces->char codes; VALUE hex pairs; exact PCM/IC/RCM/SSU length checks, RCM VIN padded7zeros.

unit_contracts.response_error_mapping: Worker init/read-save/url/file methods resolve isError booleans; server JSON requires MIR2000000. Retrieval maps saved file to intentional errorType4; no BCM backup6; read failure10; web8/offline loginMode2=>9. Write errors5 retain saveAsbuilt if reset attempted. DL005 Yes is retry only for PCM; TryAgain acknowledgments do not themselves retry.
unit_contracts.mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics: Controller stores write response.saveAsbuilt even on error; clearDtc sets sFlag before PF request. Writes set saveAsbuilt before ECU reset. Save completion deletes acnf only sFlag, then uploads or writes deferred scnf. No cancellation primitive; exits may upload before navigation. Modal disposal removes modal DOM/backdrop, normal view disposal empties panes/dispatcher; controller dispose does not initiate PF cleanup.

business_sequence: The controller constructs its base-controller state, retains commonInfo, creates an event dispatcher and ActivityLogger, and starts with model, cmnView, cmnDlg, and view set to null. Its BACK_TO_UTILITY_MENU event value is 'backToUtilityMenu'.

init constructs the local model, view factory, and dialog factory with commonInfo, logs the resource title 'Radio Silence/Dormant Mode Deactivation', and initializes the worker cache for commonInfo.getCurrentEcuId(). Only fulfillment of initialization, regardless of its value, opens the first screen. The initialization chain catches through inherited onErrorCommon.

The first screen explains the utility and instructs the user to confirm engine/power ON with Engine OFF/Ready OFF and good network coverage. These are displayed prerequisites, not programmatically tested admission conditions. Next starts resetRadioMode with a buttonless 'Please wait.' dialog. Exit opens an auto-closing Yes/No exit confirmation.

resetRadioMode starts general communication for the cached ECU and bus, requests session 0x01 and then session 0x03, and reads with {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x22,0x21,0x0C]}. A response shorter than four elements fails. A fourth element strictly equal to 0x01 retains the whole response body as savedRecord and admits a write; any other fourth element sets isNoNeed=true and skips the write and verification.

When admitted, the write is exactly {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x2E,...savedRecord.slice(1,3),0x00,...savedRecord.slice(4,savedRecord.length)]}. Its fulfilled response is not inspected. A subsequent read of [0x22,0x21,0x0C] must have at least four elements and a fourth element strictly equal to 0x00. A long-enough response with any other fourth element sets isShowDl003=true and fails.

resetRadioMode attempts to restore session 0x01 only if the session-0x03 transition fulfilled and isExtend was set. It then attempts endGeneralComm. Promise rejections of these cleanup API calls are suppressed by their helpers. The normal path returns {result:true,isNoNeed:isNoNeed,isShowDl003:isShowDl003}; the catch path performs the same cleanup sequence and returns the same fields with result:false. This is not a finally-based implementation.

The first Next handler closes the wait dialog when its model promise fulfills. A falsy resp.result selects the retry dialog if resp.isShowDl003 is truthy, otherwise inherited showCommErrorDialog. A truthy result with truthy isNoNeed logs 'The cancel is not required in this utility' and opens the not-required screen. Other truthy results open the connected-services instruction screen. This handler catches through inherited onErrorCommon, without a local dialog-closing rejection handler.
The not-required screen says that deactivation is not required because the telematics contract status is not in Radio Silence/Dormant Mode. Its Exit immediately emits the back-to-utility-menu event.

The connected-services screen tells the user to turn the engine/power switch OFF, wait 15 seconds, turn it ON with Engine OFF/Ready OFF, and wait 2 minutes. These waits and physical actions are user instructions only: the code has no timer, polling loop, elapsed-time check, or switch-state check. Its sole Next button starts initConnSvc with another buttonless wait dialog.

initConnSvc starts communication, requests sessions 0x01 and 0x03, and reads [0x22,0x21,0x0C]. It requires at least four response elements and fourth element strictly equal to 0x00. A long-enough nonzero or otherwise non-identical fourth element sets isShowDl003=true and fails. Success or failure creates {result:boolean,isShowDl003:isShowDl003}; a finally callback then always attempts session 0x01 followed by endGeneralComm, even if communication or extended-session entry failed, provided the promise chain was established.

The second Next handler closes the wait dialog on fulfillment. A falsy result with isShowDl003 opens the retry dialog. A falsy result without that flag opens inherited showCommErrorDialog and, only after that promise fulfills, recreates the first screen. A truthy result logs 'This utility is successful' and opens the completion screen. Unlike the first Next handler, this handler has no catch.

The completion screen displays 'Radio Silence/Dormant Mode Deactivation is completed.' and provides Exit, which emits the back event. The retry dialog's Yes recreates the first screen; every other pressed.id returns to the utility menu. The ordinary exit-confirmation dialog's Yes returns to the utility menu; every other pressed.id leaves the current screen unchanged.

Each screen transition disposes the current view if truthy, creates a new UtilityView through the local factory, and attaches the specified event listeners. Controller disposal disposes the current view if truthy and the controller event dispatcher, then returns a resolved promise. It does not cancel outstanding work, close dialogs, dispose the model or factories, clear worker cache, or stop native communication.

The shared framework is available at diagnostic_operations.frontend_contracts.MenuShell. gts.common transport/runtime/native behavior remains with its separate available owners. Symbolic UtilityView.ViewEvent references are exact cross-owner handoffs. EventDispatcher permits undefined event types using the same coerced property; an undefined event type does not itself prevent listener registration or delivery.

nested_functions.name: startGeneralComm
sequence: Discards fulfillment values and rejection reasons.

nested_functions.name: transitSession(modeId)
sequence: No fulfilled response predicate is applied.

nested_functions.name: beforeRead
sequence: An async function that builds {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x22,0x21,0x0C]} and awaits gts.util.SendMessageForUtility(para).then(resp=>{...}).catch(()=>Promise.reject()).
Otherwise, if resp.apiArgs.resBody[3] === 0x01, assign cacheData.savedRecord=resp.apiArgs.resBody, retaining that array reference.
Return Promise.resolve() after either accepted branch. The async function's fulfilled value is undefined.
The catch also converts failures from the fulfillment callback into a rejection without a reason.

nested_functions.name: setRadioModeByOff
sequence: The write preserves savedRecord elements at indices 1 and 2, substitutes 0x00 at outgoing index 3, and includes all savedRecord elements from index 4 onward.
Does not inspect any write response fields and does not change savedRecord to the write bytes.
The async function fulfills with undefined after the awaited chain fulfills.

nested_functions.name: afterRead
sequence: An async function that builds {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x22,0x21,0x0C]} and awaits SendMessageForUtility(para).then(resp=>{...}).catch(()=>Promise.reject()).
If resp.apiArgs.resBody.length < 4, reject without setting isShowDl003.
If resp.apiArgs.resBody[3] !== 0x00, set isShowDl003=true and reject.
Otherwise resolve. No response prefix, identifier, or trailing data is checked.
The async function fulfills with undefined after the awaited chain fulfills; its following catch also discards fulfillment-callback error reasons.

nested_functions.name: defaultSession
sequence: Async function: if !isExtend, return Promise.resolve() without calling the API.
Both API promise fulfillment and rejection fulfill the helper. It does not reset isExtend.

nested_functions.name: endGeneralComm
sequence: Passes no arguments and suppresses an API promise rejection.

branches: Only strict fourth-byte equality to 0x01 before writing admits the write; every other long-enough beforeRead response means no need, including 0x00.
A short beforeRead, read rejection, start/session rejection, or write rejection normally reaches cleanup and result:false without isShowDl003.
A short afterRead also fails without isShowDl003; a long-enough afterRead with fourth element !== 0x00 sets that flag.
isExtend is set only after successful extended-session promise fulfillment; failure to enter that session skips default-session restoration but still attempts endGeneralComm.
The catch also covers rejection arising from the normal success-cleanup chain. Such a rejection can cause cleanup to be attempted again before returning false.

The catch's own cleanup chain has no following catch. Helpers suppress returned API-promise rejections, but not all possible synchronous invocation/property errors; async helper synchronous errors become rejections and can still prevent a return object.
savedRecord is not cleared at method entry or on error; no-need and failed reads can leave an earlier savedRecord intact.
effects_and_cleanup: Attempts one read, optionally one write and one verification read; no polling, retry counter, timer, reschedule, or timer clearing.
Cleanup is sequenced defaultSession then endGeneralComm before creation of the ordinary return object.
There is no write rollback and no cancellation hook. Native fulfillment is used only as described; ECU-level success beyond the explicit response predicates is not asserted.
The complete operation chain is returned; the local nested calls are returned or awaited as specified rather than intentionally detached.

setup: Constructs new GtsPFApi(), captures model.cache.data, sets defSess=0x01, extSess=0x03, and isShowDl003=false.
Does not read param and does not track isExtend. Cache access precedes the chain.
ordered_promise_chain: Calls startGeneralComm() directly to obtain the starting promise.
catch(()=>createReturnValue(false)) converts prior promise rejections to a false-result object, ignoring the rejection reason.

business_sequence: The unit implements the browser-side 4WD Control Prevention Mode utility. Its initial screen asks the operator to confirm engine ON, vehicle stopped, parking brake applied, and shift position P for AT or N for MT. These are displayed instructions, not programmatically tested admission conditions in this unit.

The controller constructs its model, view factory, and dialog factory, logs the utility title, and initializes the worker cache using commonInfo.getCurrentEcuId(). After that initialization resolves, it displays the initial Next/Exit screen. Initialization rejection is passed to the inherited onErrorCommon handler.

The model delegates commands through $_4wd101WorkerApi to GtsWorkerApi.send. The four command strings are 4wd_101.init4wd101, 4wd_101.startExtendSession, 4wd_101.setPreventionMode, and 4wd_101.transitDefaultSession. The worker registers bound handlers for those exact strings. The shared dispatcher supplies the worker request envelope; the initialization handler reads param.parameter.ecuId.

Next immediately requests a cached, buttonless Please wait. dialog before entering the controller's try block. The controller then awaits, in order: startExtendSession, setPreventionMode, transitDefaultSession, success activity logging, loader closure, and then returns presentation of the completion screen. It does not disable Next or establish an in-flight guard.

Starting the extended session creates a GtsPFApi instance, starts general communication with the cached ecuInfo.ecuId and ecuInfo.busId, requests session modeId 1, and then requests session modeId 3. Successful shared-runtime results are ignored. A rejection in this chain leads to endGeneralComm({}), whose promise rejection is suppressed, followed by rejection with result.errorNum equal to $_4wd101.ERROR_STATUS.EXTENDSESSIONERROR, numeric 1.

The prevention-mode operation first sends {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x22,0x23,0x01]}. It inspects res.apiArgs.resBody, requires length at least 5, and tests (resBody[4] & 0b10000000) === 0b10000000. If already set, it skips both the write and delayed confirmation and resolves {}.

If the bit is initially clear, the operation takes resBody.slice(3), applies reqBodyPart[1] |= 0x80, and sends {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x2E,0x23,0x01].concat(reqBodyPart)}. It ignores the write response contents, awaits gts.util.wait(500), and sends the same read request again. Confirmation succeeds only when the response length is at least 5 and the same bit test passes. There is one delayed confirmation read, not a polling loop.

Failure of the initial read or its processing within the initial-read promise chain changes the reported error to MODECONFIRMATIONERROR, numeric 0. Write, wait, or confirmation failure retains the initial MODECHANGINGERROR, numeric 2, classification. The operation rejects an object shaped {result:{errorNum:errorNum}}; it does not restore the previous data.

The ordinary default-session operation requests transitSession({modeId:1}), suppresses its promise rejection, calls endGeneralComm() with no argument, suppresses that promise rejection, and resolves {}. Thus a resolved frontend cleanup call does not prove that either native operation succeeded.

On controller success, the activity log receives the exact resolved text This utility is successful, without a terminal period. The loader is closed and cleared, and the initial view is disposed before replacement with the completion screen. That screen states that the change is complete and instructs the operator to turn the ignition/engine switch OFF, wait 3 seconds, and turn it ON after maintenance to return to Normal mode. This unit does not execute those ignition operations or schedule that three-second wait.

The controller catches errors by directly reading e.result.errorNum. MODECHANGINGERROR=2 causes default-session cleanup, loader closure, and the dedicated failure dialog. EXTENDSESSIONERROR=1 causes loader closure and the inherited communication-error dialog without another controller default-session call. MODECONFIRMATIONERROR=0 and all other error numbers cause default-session cleanup, loader closure, and the inherited communication-error dialog. Failures inside these catch paths are not caught again here.

Exit on the initial screen opens a Yes/No confirmation. Yes emits backToUtilityMenu, No does nothing further, and an unrecognized button ID yields no explicit return from the callback. Exit on the completion screen emits backToUtilityMenu directly. Exit on the dedicated failure dialog also emits that event; any other failure-dialog button result resolves without navigation.

Controller disposal disposes only the current view, if present, and its own event dispatcher. It does not explicitly close dialogs, stop an in-flight operation, dispose the model/API, or perform communication cleanup. There are no local cancel tokens, recurring timers, timer clears, finally blocks, or automatic retry paths.

business_sequence: The unit implements the frontend workflow titled “All Seat Memory Position History Clear”. The constants namespace fragment conditionally declares an empty Zn02 function when Zn02 === undefined. The authoritative definition at characters 87652–87711 is Zn02.ERROR_STATUS=Object.freeze({CLEARERROR:0,COMERROR:1}); CLEARERROR and COMERROR are distinct numeric values 0 and 1.

Construction establishes a controller, event dispatcher, activity logger, model/API bridge, common view and dialog wrapper. Controller initialization logs the localized title, constructs those local collaborators, initializes the worker with {ecuId: commonInfo.getCurrentEcuId()}, and only after initialization fulfillment displays the introductory screen. Initialization rejection is passed to the inherited controller.onErrorCommon callback. Shared framework is available cross-owner at diagnostic_operations.frontend_contracts.MenuShell; gts.common runtime/native services are separate owners rather than missing sources.

The worker is registered as workerController.workerModels['Zn02']. Its init stores commonInfo, ecuCache and commandThread and installs four command handlers. Worker initialization reads the transported argument from param.parameter.ecuId, looks up commonInfo.getEcuInfoByEcuId(ecuId), replaces model.cache with {data:{ecuInfo}}, and resolves {}.

The introductory G001 view displays the title and r_item_i5309: “This utility is used to clear the memory position of all seat.

Confirm the following condition.
- The engine/power switch is ON (Engine OFF/Ready OFF).

Press Next to start All Seat Memory Position History Clear.” It provides Next and Exit. This condition is instructional text only: no local engine/power-state predicate or admission check is implemented.

Introductory Exit opens an auto-closing Yes/No confirmation asking “Do you want to exit the All Seat Memory Position History Clear Utility?” Yes emits backToUtilityMenu; No resolves without navigation. Unrecognized button IDs also cause no navigation.

Next first invokes the loader wrapper outside the async handler's try block and without awaiting it. The loader is titled with the utility title, says “Please wait.”, and has no buttons. The handler then sequentially awaits startExtendSession(), startHistoryClear(), and transitDefaultSession(). There is no local in-flight guard, disabling of Next, cancellation token, timeout, polling or retry timer.

startExtendSession sends the worker command zn_02.startExtendSession with {}. The worker constructs GtsPFApi, reads its cached ecuInfo, calls startGeneralComm({ecuId:ecuInfo.ecuId,busId:ecuInfo.busId}), then transitSession({modeId:1}), then transitSession({modeId:3}), and resolves {}. Fulfilled native/common-runtime values are discarded. A rejection anywhere in that promise chain attempts endGeneralComm() with no argument, suppresses that cleanup call's promise rejection, and rejects {result:{errorNum:1}}, using Zn02.ERROR_STATUS.COMERROR.

Only after extended-session setup fulfills, startHistoryClear sends zn_02.startHistoryClear with {}. Its worker calls gts.util.SendMessageForUtility({reqType:0,reqBody:[0x31,0x01,0x40,0x04]}). The bytes are exactly [49,1,64,4]. Any fulfillment is treated as success without inspecting response fields or bytes, resolving {}. Rejection becomes {result:{errorNum:0}}, using Zn02.ERROR_STATUS.CLEARERROR.

After clear fulfillment, transitDefaultSession sends zn_02.transitDefaultSession with {}. Its worker calls transitSession({modeId:1}), suppresses promise rejection from that call, then calls endGeneralComm({}), suppresses its promise rejection, and resolves {}. Thus ordinary promise rejection from either cleanup operation does not prevent the frontend success path.

On frontend success, the controller logs r_item_i5312, “This utility is successful”, calls closeLoaderDialog() without awaiting it, and replaces the introduction with the completion G001 view. That view displays “All Seat Memory Position History Clear is complete.” and provides only Exit. The controller supplies controller.inspectionMode to createZn02S002, but the view method declares no parameter and does not use it.

The Next handler catch switches directly on e.result.errorNum. CLEARERROR (numeric 0) causes another awaited transitDefaultSession(), awaited loader close, and the retry dialog. COMERROR (numeric 1) causes awaited loader close and the inherited showCommErrorDialog() without another controller-level default-session request. Any other errorNum causes awaited transitDefaultSession(), awaited loader close, and showCommErrorDialog(). No defensive validation of e or e.result and no finally block are present.

The retry dialog is titled “Error All Seat Memory Position History Clear” and says “All Seat Memory Position History Clear has failed.
Confirm the following conditions.
- The engine/power switch is ON (Engine OFF/Ready OFF).

Do you want to try again?” Both buttons auto-close. Yes merely resolves, leaving the introductory screen available for a later Next click; it does not automatically rerun the command sequence. No emits backToUtilityMenu. Other IDs produce no action.

Completion Exit emits backToUtilityMenu immediately, without a confirmation dialog. Emitting that event does not itself dispose the controller or invoke worker/native cleanup. Controller disposal disposes only the current view, if any, and its own event dispatcher, then resolves. It does not explicitly close a loader, dispose the dialog dispatcher, dispose the model/API, clear the worker cache, stop an active command, or perform session cleanup.

business_sequence: The utility is titled "Cancel Communication Function Pausing". Its introductory screen explains that it enables communication with the Center that was paused for maintenance and asks the operator to confirm engine/power switch ON with Engine OFF/Ready OFF. These are displayed instructions, not programmatically checked admission conditions.

Construction establishes controller, model, view/dialog factories, event dispatchers, activity logging, and the worker API. Controller initialization creates the model and UI factories, logs the title, initializes the worker with the current ECU ID, then shows the introductory screen. Only this initialization promise chain attaches the inherited onErrorCommon handler.

The introductory screen offers Next and Exit. Exit opens an exit-confirmation dialog; Yes triggers backToUtilityMenu and No does nothing further. Next immediately requests the Please wait loader and awaits communicationFuncPausing. There is no local busy flag, click admission guard, cancellation token, or disabling of controls.

The model sends an empty parameter object through command dcm_60.communicationFuncPausing. The worker uses ECU and bus identifiers cached by dcm_60.initDcm60. It starts general communication, requests default session with modeId 1, requests extended session with modeId 3, marks extended-session entry as successful, reads [0x22,0x20,0x43] expecting response.apiArgs.resBody[3] to be 0x01, writes [0x2E,0x20,0x43,0x00,...readValue], and reads [0x22,0x20,0x43] again expecting byte 3 to be 0x00. readValue is the first successful read's resBody.slice(4), preserved without transformation.

The worker regards response length below four or byte 3 outside the exact values 0x00 and 0x01 as COMERROR=1. An initial valid byte other than 0x01 gives NOT_REQUIRED=2 and prevents the write. A post-write valid byte other than 0x00 gives WRITE_FAILURE=3. Write response contents are not inspected. No other response-byte validation is implemented locally.

After the normal read/write/read sequence, the worker attempts default session and ends general communication. On a caught failure, it attempts default session only if the extended-session await already completed and isSessionFlg became true, then ends general communication. The normal asynchronous rejections of these cleanup calls are swallowed by their helpers. This is try/catch sequencing, not finally-based cleanup.

The returned object is {errorStatus:errorStatus}. ERROR_NONE=0 causes a success activity log, loader closure, and the completion screen. NOT_REQUIRED=2 causes a not-required activity log, loader closure, and the screen explaining that communication is already available. COMERROR=1 closes the loader and invokes inherited showCommErrorDialog(). WRITE_FAILURE=3 closes the loader and opens the retry-question dialog.

The retry-question dialog says cancellation failed, repeats the engine/power condition, and asks whether to try again. Its Yes branch merely resolves; it does not execute the operation again or replace the underlying introductory screen. No triggers backToUtilityMenu. Completion and not-required screens each offer Exit, which goes back immediately without confirmation.

No polling, timer creation, rescheduling, or timer clearing occurs in the supplied unit. Back navigation only emits an event. Disposal disposes the current view and controller event dispatcher; it does not cancel worker work, close dialogs, or dispose the model/API. Runtime/native implementations and inherited shared behavior remain separate available owners.

The authoritative constants definition freezes ERROR_STATUS with distinct numeric values 0, 1, 2, and 3. Framework behavior is cross-owned at diagnostic_operations.frontend_contracts.MenuShell; gts.common runtime/native and transport behavior likewise remains with its separate owners rather than constituting missing local source. EventDispatcher permits undefined event types through the same coerced property, so absent named event values do not establish non-delivery.

sequence: If resBody.length < 4: sets COMERROR (1) and returns Promise.reject().
If resBody[3] !== 0x00 && resBody[3] !== 0x01: sets COMERROR (1) and returns Promise.reject().
If resBody[3] !== checkParam: sets NOT_REQUIRED (2) if checkParam === 0x01, otherwise WRITE_FAILURE (3), and returns Promise.reject().
If checkParam === 0x01 after the preceding checks pass: assigns readValue=resBody.slice(4).
The following catch checks errorStatus === Dcm60.ERROR_STATUS.ERROR_NONE (0); only in that case it sets COMERROR (1). It then returns Promise.reject() with no explicit reason.
result_interpretation: Strict comparisons preserve actual runtime element types; string forms of 0 or 1 are not accepted as numeric bytes.
Does not validate response service/identifier bytes 0 through 2, exact length, trailing payload shape, or a native status field.
A length-four initial accepted response yields an empty readValue.
Exceptions inside the then callback, including missing apiArgs/resBody or slice failure, reach this catch and normally become COMERROR=1.
Explicit NOT_REQUIRED=2 and WRITE_FAILURE=3 survive the helper catch.

nested_helpers.name: setCommunicationPausing
nested_helpers.result_interpretation: Any fulfillment is accepted without checking response.apiArgs or response bytes. The preserved initial read tail is spread after 0x00. Caught rejection sets COMERROR=1.

nested_helpers.name: createReturnValue
nested_helpers.result_interpretation: No readValue, ECU fields, raw response, or original error is returned. The ordinary concrete status domain is numeric 0, 1, 2, or 3.

branches: Failure of start/default/extended steps normally selects COMERROR=1 and enters catch. If extended-session fulfillment has not completed, isSessionFlg remains false and the catch skips default-session restoration.
Initial read 0x00 selects NOT_REQUIRED=2, skips write and verification, then performs catch cleanup because isSessionFlg is true.
Initial read 0x01 preserves the tail and admits the write.
Verification read 0x01 selects WRITE_FAILURE=3; verification read 0x00 permits normal cleanup.
A fulfilled helper result is not proof of native state: only the local promise/predicate rules are represented.

Synchronous throws from API invocation or parameter construction occur before the helper's .catch is attached. If inside the outer try, they enter the outer catch without necessarily setting COMERROR. Synchronous throws during catch cleanup can escape it and prevent createReturnValue. There is no finally.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: Mutates only operation-local errorStatus, readValue, and isSessionFlg, while reading the previously populated model cache. Does not reset isSessionFlg after cleanup. No retry loop, polling, timeout, abort command, or persistent operation status is present. Asynchronous cleanup failures are deliberately swallowed; synchronous cleanup failures need not be.

guarded_ordered_transitions.sequence: See business_sequence and every member_contracts.methods entry for full ordering and branch predicates.
guarded_ordered_transitions.preparation: 001 Next -> 002; 002 Back -> 001, Next -> 003; 001/002 Exit -> exit confirmation. Screen 003 acknowledged Next logs preparation completion and shows 004.
guarded_ordered_transitions.rear: 004 Next -> loading -> startComm -> conditional RR assignment -> startRearAirBleeding -> 005, or explicit communication recovery. Screen 005 Next clears the timer and stops rear control before normal repeat confirmation; timeout clears the timer and stops rear control before the distinct timeout warning, ignoring the stop result.
guarded_ordered_transitions.rear_repeat: Normal Yes waits 1500 ms then shows 004. Normal No with exact RL logs RL completion and shows 006; any other wheel becomes RL, logs RR completion, waits twenty one-second iterations behind motor-protection progress, then starts another rear run. Timeout Yes uses the same twenty-iteration protection wait without wheel mutation; timeout No stops communication then navigates back.
guarded_ordered_transitions.front: 006 Next sets FR and starts ECB prohibition control before 007. Non-FL 007 Next closes loading, logs FR completion, sets FL, and recreates 007 without a worker request. Exact FL Next stops ECB prohibition control and requires truthy result before 008.
guarded_ordered_transitions.finish: 008 acknowledged Next logs reservoir adjustment completion and shows 009. Screen 009 Next starts a detached reset chain; either result branch stops communication. Success logs utility success and shows 010; failure shows communication error then 001. Screen 010 Exit directly triggers backToUtilityMenu.
guarded_ordered_transitions.dialog_defaults: Exit confirmation does nothing for non-YES ids. Timeout and repeat confirmations do nothing for unrecognized ids. No inferred fallback or implicit communication cleanup.

request_construction.model_api_dispatch: Model constructs {ecuId:ecuId}, {}, or {defaultSession:argument}; worker API forwards unchanged through the eight exact command strings in constant_semantics. Worker dispatch supplies param.parameter.
request_construction.default_session_shape: stopComm(false) becomes {defaultSession:false}; stopComm(true) becomes {defaultSession:true}; stopComm({defaultSession:true}) becomes {defaultSession:{defaultSession:true}}. Worker uses truthiness of param.parameter.defaultSession, not structural normalization.
request_construction.communication_stop: Conditionally transitSession({modeId:0x01}) when defaultSession is truthy, then stopKeepAlive(), endGeneralComm(), and cacheData.startComm=false.
request_construction.reset: Send {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x22,0x20,0x02]}; require at least five response bytes; alias that complete resBody as reqBody, assign byte 0=0x2E and byte 4=byte 4 & 0x7F; send the complete aliased array; wait 1000 ms; reread with [0x22,0x20,0x02].
request_construction.no_inferred_native_internals: Typed local handoffs are preserved. No additional native payload, serialization normalization, response rewriting, or vehicle effect is asserted.

response_error_mapping.startup: Already-started cache -> {result:true,executed:true}; fresh successful sequence -> {result:true,executed:false}; chain rejection -> {result:false,executed:false}. Negative-response-condition asynchronous rejection is ignored. Synchronous setup before the promise chain remains outside its catch.
response_error_mapping.shutdown: Individual asynchronous helper fulfillments and rejections are ignored; successful sequence clears the cache flag and returns {result:true}. Synchronous invocation errors or malformed params can prevent subsequent cleanup; no outer catch.
response_error_mapping.utility_controls: Strict resultInfo.result === 0 and resBody.length >= 5 are required, without checking response byte patterns. Chain rejections and callback exceptions map to {result:false}; success maps to {result:true}.
response_error_mapping.reset: All sends require strict resultInfo.result === 0. Initial read requires length >= 5; write has no body-length/content predicate; final read requires length >= 5 and byte 4 bit 0x80 clear. Chain failures map to {result:false}.

business_sequence: Initialize the Brake Line Air Bleeding utility using commonInfo.getCurrentEcuId(). Construct the model, view factory, and dialog factory, log the title resource r_item_i5160, initialize the worker cache for that ECU, and display S_ABS-102-001. Initialization catches rejected promises with inherited onErrorCommon; the synchronous setup before Promise.resolve() is outside that catch.

Preparation consists of an informational screen, acknowledgment that the reservoir filler cap has been removed, and acknowledgment that the reservoir has been refilled to MAX. The informational resources state engine/power ON with engine/Ready OFF, battery 12–14 V, parking brake applied, shift P, fluid between MIN/MAX, and the possibility of DTCs requiring later clearing. These are displayed instructions, not measured admission predicates in this unit. The checkbox acknowledgments enforce one-way UI progression. After preparation, log r_item_i5162 and display rear-bleeding instructions.

On rear-bleeding admission, display the buttonless Please wait dialog, call startComm(), and require a truthy response.result. If response.executed is falsy, set wheel='RR'. The worker's executed field is true when communication was already marked started and false when it performs the startup sequence; preserve this naming and interpretation. Start rear bleeding using request [0x31,0x01,0x11,0x69] after a 1000 ms wait. A successful worker result permits the timed rear-wheel screen.

Each rear-wheel run starts a 120-second interval-based countdown. The operator acknowledges opening/closing the selected RR or RL bleeder and then closing the plug. Only after the second acknowledgment is Next enabled. Clicking Next clears the interval and stops rear bleeding with [0x31,0x02,0x11,0x69], then asks whether to repeat. Timeout clears the interval, sends the same stop request, ignores its result field, and instead asks whether to retry after exceeding 120 seconds.

A timeout retry shows a 20-second motor-protection progress dialog before restarting rear bleeding. Declining that retry stops communication and exits to the utility menu. A normal repeat confirmation Yes waits 1500 ms behind Please wait and returns to the rear instruction screen; a subsequent Next invokes startComm again. Normal confirmation No after RR changes wheel to RL, logs RR completion, waits 20 seconds for motor protection, and starts another rear run. Normal confirmation No when wheel is exactly RL logs RL completion and proceeds to front instructions.

Front admission sets wheel='FR', requests ECB prohibition control using [0x31,0x01,0x11,0x35] after a 1000 ms wait, and displays the FR instructions if successful. Four sequential one-way checkbox acknowledgments cover holding the pedal, opening the selected front bleeder and pressing fully, closing/releasing, and waiting more than one second. The source does not time that last acknowledgment. A fifth text instruction says to repeat until air stops. FR Next logs completion and switches to FL without a worker request. FL Next stops ECB prohibition control with [0x31,0x02,0x11,0x35], requires a truthy result, logs completion, and proceeds.

Acknowledge reservoir fluid at MAX, log r_item_i5167, and proceed to vacuum-filling-incomplete-flag reset. Reset reads [0x22,0x20,0x02], requires at least five returned bytes, mutates the returned array in place by setting byte 0 to 0x2E and clearing bit 0x80 in byte 4, and sends that entire mutated array. After 1000 ms it rereads and requires at least five bytes with byte 4 bit 0x80 clear. Successful reset is followed by stopComm, success logging, and the Complete screen. The controller reset click handler starts but does not return its promise chain.

Worker communication startup requests general communication, marks cache.data.startComm=true, starts keepalive, sets {repReqRetryMax:0}, and transits sessions 0x01 then 0x03. Most startup failures become {result:false,executed:false}; the negative-response-condition promise rejection is deliberately ignored. stopComm optionally requests session 0x01 based on truthiness of its incoming defaultSession field, then stops keepalive, ends general communication, clears the cache flag, and returns {result:true}; its individual asynchronous API failures are ignored.

Several controller failure branches stop the active control, stop communication, close the tracked progress/loading dialog, show inherited showCommErrorDialog(), and return to the first screen. There is no shared local finally, cancellation token, reentry lock, or universal cleanup. dispose() disposes the current view and event dispatcher only: it does not clear the countdown, close dialogs, stop controls, or stop communication. Native/common-runtime calls are requests and response interpretations, not evidence of completed vehicle operations.

semantics: Synchronously construct new GtsPFApi() and read model.cache.data. Return Promise.resolve().then(()=>{...}).catch(()=>createReturnValue(false,false)).
If cacheData.startComm is truthy, return createReturnValue(true,true) without calling any platform startup methods.

Otherwise return Promise.resolve().then(startGeneralComm).then(()=>{cacheData.startComm=true;}).then(startKeepAlive).then(setNegativeResponseCondition).then(()=>transitSession(0x01)).then(()=>transitSession(0x03)).then(()=>createReturnValue(true,false)).

Nested startGeneralComm sends {ecuId:cacheData.ecuInfo.ecuId,busId:cacheData.ecuInfo.busId} to gtsPFApi.startGeneralComm. Its response callback resolves only when response.resultInfo.result === 0; otherwise rejects.
Nested startKeepAlive calls gtsPFApi.startKeepAlive() and uses the same === 0 predicate.

Nested setNegativeResponseCondition calls gtsPFApi.setNegativeResponseCondition({repReqRetryMax:0}). Both fulfillment and rejection callbacks return Promise.resolve(), ignoring the result and asynchronous failure.
Nested transitSession(modeId) calls gtsPFApi.transitSession({modeId:modeId}) and requires response.resultInfo.result === 0.
Nested createReturnValue(result,executed) returns Promise.resolve({result:result,executed:executed}). Any chain rejection reaches catch and becomes {result:false,executed:false}.
branches: The cache flag is set before keepalive, negative-response configuration, and session transitions. Later failure does not reset it.

Synchronous setup failures before Promise.resolve() are outside the catch. A synchronous throw while invoking setNegativeResponseCondition is not swallowed by that helper's rejection callback, but is caught by the outer chain.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: No automatic stop/rollback on startup failure. The executed flag true means cached/already-started, not freshly executed.

semantics: Return Promise.resolve().then(()=>sendMessage([0x22,0x20,0x02]).then(response=>{if(response.apiArgs.resBody.length < 5){return Promise.reject();}return Promise.resolve(response.apiArgs.resBody);})).

Then receive resBody, assign var reqBody=resBody without copying, set reqBody[0]=0x2E and reqBody[4]=reqBody[4] & 0x7F, and return sendMessage(reqBody). Preserve every other byte and the original array length.
Then await gts.util.wait(1000) in an async callback.
Then sendMessage([0x22,0x20,0x02]) and reject if response.apiArgs.resBody.length < 5 || response.apiArgs.resBody[4] & 0x80. Otherwise the callback returns undefined and fulfills.
Then createReturnValue(true); catch any chain rejection and createReturnValue(false).

Nested sendMessage(reqBody) calls gts.util.SendMessageForUtility({reqType:0,reqBody:reqBody}); resolve with the original response only if response.resultInfo.result === 0, otherwise reject. Nested createReturnValue(result) returns Promise.resolve({result:result}).

The final bit test uses bitwise AND with 0x80; no other returned bytes are compared.
Malformed responses causing callback exceptions become false through the catch.

Routes {} to worker startComm; returns result and executed with the documented cached-versus-fresh interpretation.
Routes {defaultSession:argument} unchanged; worker tests truthiness at param.parameter.defaultSession.
Routes {} to the delayed rear-control start request.
Routes {} to the rear-control stop request without a pre-send wait.
Routes {} to delayed ECB prohibition control start.
Routes {} to ECB prohibition control stop without a pre-send wait.

Shared property used for rendered Next button ids and controller event registrations. Preserve its shared definition without substituting an invented string.
Shared property used for rendered Back button ids and the screen 002 Back listener; later Back controls are disabled as documented.
Shared property used for rendered Exit button ids and screen 001/002/010 listeners; exit confirmation applies only to 001/002.
Confirmation button id and switch case. Exit Yes navigates back; timeout Yes waits for motor protection then restarts; repeat Yes waits 1500 ms then shows 004.
Confirmation button id. Exit No has no navigation; timeout No shuts down and exits; repeat No advances RR-to-RL or exact RL-to-front.

Undefined event types are permitted and use the same coerced property key for registration and triggering. Do not infer failed delivery solely from an undefined event value or assert distinct keys without the shared definitions.
Startup requests 0x01 then 0x03; shutdown optionally requests 0x01. The retry-setting request has exactly {repReqRetryMax:0}, and its asynchronous rejection is ignored.

Control requests require strict result 0 and at least five bytes, without positive-byte-pattern validation. Reset aliases the initial body, changes byte 0 to 0x2E, clears bit 0x80 of byte 4 with 0x7F, and later verifies that bit is clear.

Rear countdown is interval-based, not wall-clock compensated. Motor protection renders 0 then each 1–20 before its respective awaited second. The displayed front wait-more-than-one-second instruction has no corresponding timer.

resource_binding.presentation_source: Unit view/dialog methods construct inline DOM or supply typed content/button/table parameters to shared UtilityView/createCommonDialog; no external workflow HTML template path is referenced by these members. Exact inline HTML and options are preserved in source evidence.

entry_admission.initialization: Controller init is externally invoked with initArgs, which is ignored. It initializes the worker cache before creating G001. Worker registration occurs only when workerController.workerModels['Dcm61'] is falsy.
entry_admission.history_read: G001 Next opens the loader and starts a history read without a busy guard, duplicate-click suppression, cancellation check or vehicle-state check.
entry_admission.instruction_not_predicate: The engine/power switch ON (Engine OFF/Ready OFF) condition is instructional resource text, not an executable admission predicate.

input_domain.strictness: Controller status switches and view support selection use strict matching. Every supportType other than numeric 0 selects the view's CN branch.

guarded_ordered_transitions: init: construct model/view/dialog factories → title log → await worker initialization through the returned chain → create G001 → inherited onErrorCommon catch on rejection.

Next: synchronously open loader → await history request → strict status routing. Status 0 logs success, closes loader and detaches history-view creation; status 1 closes loader and invokes shared communication-error UI; status 2 closes loader and detaches the no-data dialog; other statuses leave the loader unchanged.

Worker: cached ECU/bus → startGeneralComm → session 1 → session 3 → mark extended-session flag → discover support → select JP before CN → sequential supported history requests in table order → best-effort session 1 → best-effort endGeneralComm → final status.
Main worker failure: restore session 1 only if the extended-session flag was set → best-effort endGeneralComm → COMERROR=1, subject to synchronous cleanup exceptions.
History rendering: all common rows and fields in order → JP's nine additional columns/fields for supportType===0, otherwise CN's three sensor columns/fields → shared L002 initialization.
Intro Exit → confirmation → Yes emits backToUtilityMenu; No does not navigate. History Exit and no-data Ok emit backToUtilityMenu directly.

request_construction.history_reads: Exactly {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x22,0x10,supportDID]}, with supportDID selected from the worker method's exact JP/CN table and only when its support bit is set.

response_error_mapping.support: response.apiArgs.resBody.length<17 rejects discovery; otherwise masks at indices 13/14 choose JP first, then indices 15/16 choose CN, otherwise SUPPORT_NONE=2. No positive-service or DID-echo predicate is present.
response_error_mapping.individual_history: Length<95 for DIDs with (supportDID & 0xF0)===0x50, or length<82 otherwise, maps to VALID_DATA_NONE=2 for that read. Send rejection or an exception in its fulfillment callback also maps locally to 2 and fulfills, so later reads continue.
response_error_mapping.normal_completion: Any collected row produces ERROR_NONE=0. No selected family or an empty collected list produces VALID_DATA_NONE=2.
response_error_mapping.main_failure: Main-try failure produces COMERROR=1 after the specified cleanup. Pre-try failures and synchronous exceptions escaping cleanup can instead reject the async method.
response_error_mapping.controller: Exact per-case order and detached-promise semantics are retained in onClickSDcm61001ViewNextBtn.

mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.cache: Initialization replaces worker cache and copies only ecuId and busId. History reads use that initialized cache, not a new request ECU identifier.
mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.view: Screen replacement disposes the old truthy view. History assignment occurs only after asynchronous creation succeeds; rejection leaves the old disposed view reference in place.
mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.modal: Opening a loader closes and nulls a truthy controller.modalView before assigning the new loader. closeLoaderDialog closes and nulls only cmnDlg.loaderDlg, leaving controller.modalView potentially stale.
mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.dispose: Directly calls current view.disposeView(), then eventDisp.dispose(), with no null guard, modal/model/API disposal, field clearing or cancellation.
mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.communication: Normal and main-catch paths attempt session/communication cleanup as specified in the worker method; there is no finally and no explicit PFApi disposal.

mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.timers: No local polling, timers, rescheduling, retry loop or timer clearing.

business_sequence: The constants member conditionally declares an empty Dcm61 constructor when Dcm61 === undefined. It assigns frozen ERROR_STATUS={ERROR_NONE:0,COMERROR:1,VALID_DATA_NONE:2} and frozen SUPPORT_TYPE={DID1053_105A_SUPPORT:0,DID1063_106A_SUPPORT:1,SUPPORT_NONE:2}. Both exact definitions are authoritative supplied source facts.

Controller construction initializes the base controller, stores commonInfo, creates an event dispatcher and ActivityLogger, and initializes model, cmnVIew, cmnDlg, view and modalView to null. The spelling cmnVIew is distinct from the cmnView property assigned by init.

Controller init constructs the model, common view factory and dialog factory, logs the title 'HELPNET Notification History', then calls model.initDcm61(controller). The model ignores that extra argument and sends {ecuId: commonInfo.getCurrentEcuId()} using worker command 'dcm_61.initDcm61'. The worker obtains ECU information from param.parameter.ecuId and replaces its cache with {data:{ecuInfo:{ecuId:ecuInfo.ecuId,busId:ecuInfo.busId}}}. Only after that promise fulfills does the controller create the introductory screen. The init promise chain catches through the inherited onErrorCommon function.

The G001 introductory screen displays the HELPNET history purpose and asks the operator to confirm engine/power switch ON with Engine OFF/Ready OFF. This condition is instructional text only: no local code tests ignition, engine or readiness state. Next and Exit are wired to controller callbacks; no local busy guard or duplicate-click suppression is installed.

Next first opens a buttonless 'Please wait.' dialog, then awaits model.helpNortificationHistoryData(), which sends an empty object using command 'dcm_61.helpNortificationHistoryData'. The worker uses the cache established by initialization; it does not consume a new ECU identifier from this request.

The worker starts general communication with the cached ECU and bus identifiers, requests modeId 1, then modeId 3, and only after successful extended-session transition sets its isSessionFlg=true. It sends {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x22,0xA1,0x10]} and examines response.apiArgs.resBody. Responses shorter than 17 reject support discovery. JP support has precedence when either (resBody[13] & 0x1F) !== 0 or (resBody[14] & 0xE0) !== 0; otherwise CN support is selected when either corresponding test on bytes 15 and 16 succeeds. The support bitmap is resBody.slice(3).

For the selected support family, the worker visits its eight bitmap entries in ascending table order and sequentially awaits only the supported history requests. JP requests use [0x22,0x10,0x53] through [0x22,0x10,0x5A]; CN requests use [0x22,0x10,0x63] through [0x22,0x10,0x6A]. A JP response requires length at least 95 and a CN response at least 82. Failed or short individual reads become VALID_DATA_NONE=2 locally and do not abort later reads. A response of sufficient length is retained whole, including its first three bytes; there is no service/header/content-validity predicate before collection.

After discovery and reads, the worker awaits a best-effort modeId 1 transition and best-effort endGeneralComm. An empty collected list, or no supported family, yields VALID_DATA_NONE=2; any nonempty list yields ERROR_NONE=0 despite failed sibling reads. An exception in the main try path invokes best-effort default-session restoration only if isSessionFlg is true, then best-effort endGeneralComm, and sets COMERROR=1. There is no finally block. The result is {comResult:errorStatus,supportType:supportType,dataFormat:gts.util.dateFormatId,supportList:supportList.concat()}.

On ERROR_NONE=0, the controller logs 'This utility is successful', closes the loader through the dialog factory, and starts creating the history screen without awaiting or returning that creation promise. On COMERROR=1 it closes the loader and calls inherited showCommErrorDialog() with no arguments. On VALID_DATA_NONE=2 it closes the loader and opens the no-history dialog; its Ok response navigates back. Any other comResult leaves the loader unchanged. Rejection of the awaited history request has no local catch or finally.

The L002 history screen first builds all common rows sequentially, then appends JP-specific telematics and seven sensor columns when supportType === 0, or only three CN sensor columns for every other supportType. It decodes at header-relative offsets with RECV_HEADER_LEN=3. Except the notification-history type, each displayed decoded field requires the row byte at 3+1 to be exactly 0x01; otherwise it displays resource r_item_i5465, '-'. A collected row with that byte unset can therefore still reach the successful history screen.

Date fields interpret each byte as two padded hexadecimal characters, reject nondecimal character strings and specified byte-range violations, construct a UTC Date and display local-time date parts in the requested dataFormat ordering. There is no full calendar-validity check. Counts use unsigned typed reads, telephone bytes are expanded high nibble then low nibble, and enumeration/sensor values map to supplied resources as detailed in the view method contract.

Introductory Exit opens an auto-closing Yes/No confirmation; Yes triggers 'backToUtilityMenu', No does nothing further. History-screen Exit immediately triggers that event without confirmation. No-data Ok also triggers it. Navigation emits an event and returns a fulfilled promise; it does not itself dispose the view or cancel worker work.

Controller disposal directly disposes the current view and event dispatcher, then returns a fulfilled promise. It does not guard a null view, close a modal, dispose the dialog/model/API or cancel an in-flight request. No local method installs polling, timers, rescheduling or timer clearing.

Shared framework behavior is available cross-owner at diagnostic_operations.frontend_contracts.MenuShell. gts.common runtime and native owners are separate available owners rather than missing local sources. EventDispatcher permits undefined event types by using the same coerced property key; an undefined event value does not by itself prevent registration or delivery.

business_sequence: The unit implements Steering Control Actuator Adjust. The initial screen presents engine/power ON with Engine OFF/Ready OFF, vehicle stopped, shift in P, and steering centered as operator instructions. These conditions are not programmatically checked by this unit.

Controller initialization constructs the model, view factory, and dialog factory; initializes worker cache using commonInfo.getCurrentEcuId(); logs the utility title; and shows screen 001. The init result payload is not inspected.

Screen 001 Next starts general communication, keep-alive, default session, and extended session in that order, then requests dealer mode. A startup or dealer-transition error leads to the inherited communication-error dialog. Following successful transition, the controller displays the cancellable processing dialog and waits for dealer-mode status.

Dealer status requests wait 50 before each request and repeat only while response byte 4 is 0x01. Byte 0x02 means success. Cancellation is tested before each wait, not again between the wait and request. A cancellation-confirmation deferred can delay delivery of the status result to the controller.

After successful dealer status, the controller reads DID [0x20,0x18], replaces the first byte of its returned data with 0x00, writes that data back, requests steering-zero-point hold mode, and checks hold status. The hold-status implementation performs at most one request: its loop flag is never set true. Only byte 4 equal to 0x01 succeeds.

Screen 002 instructs toe inspection, prohibits door operation and power-off, and asks the operator to continue if inspection is within reference or exit and perform toe adjustment otherwise. Next releases hold mode and ends the extended session, then shows screen 003 on success. Exit confirmation ends the session, displays the finished/power-cycle message, and returns to the utility menu.

Screen 003 says toe adjustment is complete and requests a power OFF/ON cycle. Next starts another extended session, transitions to dealer mode, checks dealer status through the cancellable-processing flow, and shows screen 004 on success. This code does not detect the instructed power cycle.
Screen 004 asks for a test drive without steering load and checking vehicle deviation. Next resets the adjustment counter to zero and shows screen 005.

Screen 005 displays adjustment instructions, a power-off warning, the signed-direction counter, and left/right/Next buttons. Left uses DID [0x20,0x16]; right uses DID [0x20,0x17]. Each operation reads the selected DID, changes the first returned data byte to zero, and writes it back. Only successful writes decrement or increment the frontend counter. A write rejection with errorCode strictly equal to 'VC000003' and detailCode strictly equal to 'NRC22' sets both isExceededValue and isError; the controller prioritizes the exceeded-value path, ends the session, shows the acceptable-value warning, then returns to the menu.

Screen 005 Next ends the session, logs a resource-derived successful result using the absolute counter and direction, and shows screen 006. Screen 006 states completion and requests power OFF/ON; Exit emits backToUtilityMenu.

Processing cancellation opens a Yes/No confirmation. Yes sets frontend isCancel and worker cache isCancel to true before resolving the deferred. No reopens the processing dialog and resolves the deferred. The controller later prioritizes isCancel over the worker isError result, ends the session, displays the finished message, then returns to the menu.

Retry after a failure returns to screen 001 without reinitializing worker cache. Starting either processing flow resets only controller.isCancel, not worker cache.isCancel or controller.def. This preserves a worker-cancellation latch after confirmed cancellation unless initEmps13 runs again.

The unit owns no explicit timer handles, timeout limits, or timer clearing. Its only polling delay is gts.util.wait(50). Controller dispose only disposes the current view and event dispatcher; it does not cancel polling, close dialogs, or terminate communication.
