methods.effects_and_cleanup: No command admission or serialization policy is implemented here.

methods.semantics: Reads ecuId=param.parameter.ecuId; resolves ecuInfo=model.commonInfo.getEcuInfoByEcuId(ecuId); forms cache={data:{ecuInfo:ecuInfo,isCancel:false}}; assigns model.cache=cache; returns Promise.resolve() without a payload.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: Replaces the entire utility cache and resets worker cancellation. No ECU-info validation or local catch.

semantics: Constructs new GtsPFApi(); reads cacheData=model.cache.data; sets isError=true before the try.
Try awaits nested startGeneralComm(), startKeepAlive(), transitDefaultSession(), and transitExtendedSession() in order, then sets isError=false.
startGeneralComm sends {ecuId:cacheData.ecuInfo.ecuId,busId:cacheData.ecuInfo.busId} to gtsPFApi.startGeneralComm. Its then discards the result and resolves undefined; catch rejects without a reason.
startKeepAlive sends {} to gtsPFApi.startKeepAlive, then resolves undefined or rejects without a reason through its then/catch.
transitDefaultSession sends {modeId:1} to gtsPFApi.transitSession, then resolves undefined or rejects without a reason.
transitExtendedSession sends {modeId:3} to gtsPFApi.transitSession, then resolves undefined or rejects without a reason.

Catch awaits stopKeepAlive(), then endGeneralComm(). stopKeepAlive calls gtsPFApi.stopKeepAlive() with no argument; endGeneralComm calls gtsPFApi.endGeneralComm() with no argument. Each converts both fulfillment and rejection of the returned promise into fulfilled undefined.
Returns nested createReturnValue(), which resolves {isError:isError}.
branches: Any awaited startup rejection skips remaining startup operations and leaves isError=true.
Failure cleanup does not transit back to default session.
Construction and model.cache.data access occur outside try.
Promise catches do not protect synchronous throws occurring before a promise chain is created.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: Successful startup leaves keep-alive and communication active. No finally.

methods.semantics: Sets isError=true. Try awaits nested transitDealerMode(), then sets false; empty catch preserves true. The nested function calls SendMessageForUtility({reqType:0,reqBody:[0x31,0x01,0x10,0x02]}), then resolves undefined on fulfillment and rejects without a reason on rejection. createReturnValue resolves {isError:isError}.
branches: Any fulfilled response is accepted; no response bytes are inspected.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: No session cleanup within this method.

semantics: Sets isError=true; captures cache=model.cache.data; awaits nested checkDealerModeStatus(); returns createReturnValue() resolving {isError:isError}.

The nested checker initializes isStandby=false and enters a do/while. Each iteration resets isStandby=false; if cache.isCancel is truthy, breaks immediately; otherwise awaits gts.util.wait(50), then awaits sendMessage().
Switch on routineStatus: case 0x02 sets isError=false; case 0x01 sets isStandby=true; default changes neither. The loop repeats only while isStandby.
sendMessage creates {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x31,0x03,0x10,0x02]} and routineStatus=undefined. It calls SendMessageForUtility(para).then(result => ...).

The response callback rejects without a reason if result.apiArgs.resBody.length < 5; otherwise assigns routineStatus=result.apiArgs.resBody[4] and resolves undefined. Its catch swallows rejection into fulfilled undefined; a final then resolves routineStatus.
branches: 0x01 repeats after another wait(50); 0x02 succeeds and stops; all other values, malformed short responses, and send rejections stop with isError=true.
Cancellation before an iteration leaves isError=true.
Cancellation arriving during wait does not prevent that iteration's request.
No top-level catch handles wait rejection or other escaping failures.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: No timeout, iteration cap, timer handle, or clear operation. Cancellation is not reset.

semantics: Sets isError=true and readData=[]. Try awaits readSteeringZeroPointOffset(), then writeSteeringZeroPointOffset(), then sets isError=false. Empty catch preserves true. Returns createReturnValue() resolving {isError:isError}.

Read sends {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x22,0x20,0x18]}. Its then obtains result.apiArgs.resBody; length < 4 returns Promise.reject(); otherwise readData=resBody.slice(3) and resolves undefined. Its catch rejects without a reason.

Write aliases writeData=readData, sets writeData[0]=0x00, and sends {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x2E,0x20,0x18,...writeData]}. Its then accepts any fulfillment and resolves undefined; catch rejects without a reason.
branches: Read failure prevents the write.
All data bytes after response index 3 are preserved except the first sliced byte, which is replaced by zero.
No response-prefix, DID echo, or positive-write-body validation is performed locally.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: The sliced array is mutated through its alias. No cache update or session cleanup.

methods.semantics: Sets isError=true. Try awaits nested transitSteeringZeroPointHoldMode() then sets false; empty catch preserves true. Nested send uses {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x31,0x01,0x11,0x10]}; then resolves undefined for any fulfillment, catch rejects without a reason. createReturnValue resolves {isError:isError}.
branches: No response-body predicates.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: No local session cleanup.

semantics: Sets isError=true; captures cache=model.cache.data; awaits nested checker; returns createReturnValue() resolving {isError:isError}.
Checker initializes isStandby=false, enters do/while, resets isStandby=false, breaks if cache.isCancel, otherwise awaits gts.util.wait(50), then sendMessage().
Switch accepts only case 0x01, setting isError=false. Default does nothing. No branch ever sets isStandby=true, so the loop never repeats.

sendMessage uses {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x31,0x03,0x11,0x10]} and routineStatus=undefined. Its then rejects if result.apiArgs.resBody.length < 5; otherwise takes byte 4 and resolves undefined. Catch swallows rejection; final then resolves routineStatus.
branches: At most one request occurs; an already-cancelled cache causes zero requests.
Only exact status 0x01 succeeds. All other statuses, short responses, and send rejections yield isError=true.
Cancellation during wait does not suppress that iteration's request.
No top-level catch for wait rejection.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: Preserves the source's non-rescheduling loop anomaly. No timer handle or clear.

methods.semantics: Sets isError=true. Try awaits nested releaseSteeringZeroPointHoldMode() then sets false; empty catch preserves true. Nested send uses {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x31,0x02,0x11,0x10]}; then resolves undefined for any fulfillment, catch rejects without a reason. createReturnValue resolves {isError:isError}.
branches: No response-body predicates.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: Does not itself end the session.

semantics: Initializes isError=false, isExceededValue=false, targetDid=param.parameter.targetDid, readData=[]. Input access occurs before try.

Outer try awaits readSteeringAngleOffset(). Inner try then awaits writeSteeringAngleOffset(). Inner catch tests e.isNr22; if truthy sets isExceededValue=true; then throws Error(''). Outer catch sets isError=true.

Read sends {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x22,...targetDid]}. Its then obtains result.apiArgs.resBody; length < 4 rejects; otherwise readData=resBody.slice(3), then resolves undefined. Catch rejects without a reason.
Write aliases writeData=readData, sets writeData[0]=0x00, then sends {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x2E,...targetDid,...writeData]}. Its success callback ignores result and resolves undefined.

Write catch receives response, initializes isNr22=false, and tests response.errorCode === gts.ERROR_CODE.NEGATIVE_RESPONSE && response.detailCode === gts.DETAIL_CODE.CONDITIONS_NOT_CORRECT. The authoritative constants resolve to string 'VC000003' and string 'NRC22', respectively. If both strict comparisons hold, sets isNr22=true. Rejects {isNr22:isNr22}.
createReturnValue resolves {isError:isError,isExceededValue:isExceededValue}.
branches: Successful read and write produce {isError:false,isExceededValue:false}.
Read failures produce {isError:true,isExceededValue:false} without writing.
The classified write rejection produces {isError:true,isExceededValue:true}; other ordinary write rejections produce {isError:true,isExceededValue:false}.

If the rejection object is null/undefined, the classifier's property access can throw; the outer catch still sets isError=true, without a normalized rejection object. Shared constants are defined by the supplied frozen definitions.
No DID-length, target range, response prefix, or numeric adjustment-limit validation.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: Only the first sliced data byte is zeroed; all remaining data is spread unchanged. No counter mutation occurs in the worker.

semantics: Constructs new GtsPFApi(); returns transitDefaultSession().then(stopKeepAlive).then(endGeneralComm).then(createReturnValue).
transitDefaultSession sends {modeId:1} to gtsPFApi.transitSession; its then and catch both resolve undefined.
stopKeepAlive creates {} and passes it to gtsPFApi.stopKeepAlive(para); its then and catch both resolve undefined.
endGeneralComm calls gtsPFApi.endGeneralComm() with no argument; its then and catch both resolve undefined.
createReturnValue resolves {}.
branches: Ordinary promise rejections from each native-facing call are swallowed, allowing the next cleanup stage.
Synchronous throws before attaching a promise catch are not covered by that catch.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: No cancellation reset, cache clearing, or explicit hold-release operation. The returned {} does not report cleanup success.

methods.semantics: Reads cacheData=model.cache.data; assigns cacheData.isCancel=param.parameter.isCancel; returns Promise.resolve() without payload.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: No Boolean coercion or direct interruption of an outstanding wait/send. Checkers observe the shared cache property at their next pre-wait test.

member_contracts.semantics: All supplied referenced resources are accounted for in the view, dialog, title-log, counter-format, and result-log contracts. Message types are c for confirmations, i for finished information, l for waiting screens, and w for failure warnings. Button result id 'Ok' is distinct from displayed label 'OK'.

resource_binding.presentation_source: Unit view/dialog methods construct inline DOM or supply typed content/button/table parameters to shared UtilityView/createCommonDialog; no external workflow HTML template path is referenced by these members. Exact inline HTML and options are preserved in source evidence.

entry_admission.startup: Csn11Controller(commonInfo) captures commonInfo.getCurrentEcuId(); init constructs the model, dialog and view factory, resolves resources, dispatches worker initialization without awaiting it, logs the title, and shows S001.
entry_admission.operator_instructions: S001 asks for engine/power ON with Engine OFF/Ready OFF, a stopped vehicle, and selection of replaced or removed parts. It warns against IG OFF after Next. These are displayed conditions, not measured admission predicates.
entry_admission.screen_guards: S001 enables Next if any checkbox is checked. S002 initially disables Next and subsequently enables it on input when the current textbox value is nonempty. S003 has no local measured-condition guard or Next disablement.
entry_admission.worker_registration: All worker definitions and final registration are guarded by !workerController.workerModels['Csn11']; a truthy existing registration skips the entire block.
entry_admission.reentrancy: No local operation-in-progress or controller Next-handler reentrancy guard exists.

input_domain.initialization: {ecuId} is passed unchanged through model/API initialization; the worker consumes param.parameter.ecuId and obtains ECU info through commonInfo?.getEcuInfoByEcuId.
input_domain.selection: customEvent.args[1] is an ordered collection of {domId,value} records. All records are retained and logged; only customEvent.args[1][0].value becomes {checked}. Worker branching uses truthiness; checkbox restoration requires value === true.
input_domain.bumper: The UI filters ASCII/full-width digits, truncates to two characters and converts full-width digits outside composition. The controller sends the current value unchanged as {bumperType}; the worker applies parseInt(value,10). There is no worker minimum/finiteness validation.
input_domain.responses: Platform checked operations consume result.resultInfo.result. Utility reads consume fulfilled result.apiArgs.resBody through the local adapter. Raw failure rows are {did,resBody}; frontend rows are ordered arrays of resolved display values.
input_domain.dialogs: Controller callbacks inspect pressed.id with exact case-sensitive IDs Yes, No, Ok and Cancel. Dialog constants also define unused common-error IDs OK.

state_fields.controller: commonInfo, eventDisp, activityReport, model, cmnDlg, view, modalView, ecuId, dl006BtnPressed, S001CheckedStatus; init additionally creates csn11View and resets screenNumber, S001CheckedStatus and dl006BtnPressed to null.
state_fields.frontend_model: commonInfo, api, RESOURCE_IDS and RESOURCES; RESOURCES is assigned by initCsn11 before the worker initialization send.
state_fields.view_factory: eventDisp, $viewPane=$('#v_pane'), $ctrlPane=$('#v_c_pane'), screen004CheckBoxState=[], RESOURCES. Pane references and checkbox-state array are not used by supplied prototype methods.
state_fields.worker: commandHandler={}, buffer=null, commonInfo=null, ecuCache=null, cache=null, commandThread=null, storedCache=null at construction. init sets bumperType=0, cancelFlag=false and runtime owner references; initCsn11 sets ecuInfo and cache={data:{}}. Bumper-write processing uses a local bumperType and does not update model.bumperType.
state_fields.polling_locals: _loop, _ret, support parsers, supported DID lists and raw response lists are local to phase 2. No interval or timeout handle is retained.

guarded_ordered_transitions: Startup -> S001 without awaiting worker initialization. S001 Next logs all parts, opens DL001 and sends {checked}. Successful checked-truthy processing -> S002; successful checked-falsy processing -> S003.

S002 Next logs Bumper Type plus unchanged input, opens DL001, parses/range-checks/writes/readbacks in the worker, then closes DL001 before routing. SUCCESS -> S003; RETYPE_BUMPER_TYPE -> DL004. DL004 Ok explicitly ends session/communication and redisplays a fresh S002.

S003 Next -> DL001 -> phase 1. Admission success leaves communication active; the controller replaces DL001 with cancellable DL005 and awaits phase 2. Nonzero initialization-condition failure -> cleanup, report and S004; S004 Try Again -> S003 without a request until Next.

Phase 2 waits 200 milliseconds before each status read. Completed-only -> normal-mode/session/communication cleanup -> SUCCESS or OCCURED_COMMUNICATIN_ERROR_S001. Nonterminal status -> another iteration. Terminal failed/completed mix -> normal mode, session 1, supported bus reads and optionally supported sensor reads in ascending candidate order -> S005 or S006 after communication termination.

DL005 Cancel -> DL006 plus stored deferred promise. Yes -> DL001, detached changeCancelFlag, resolve Yes; No -> new DL005, resolve No. Phase-2 completion additionally waits for the currently stored confirmation promise. Yes overrides every result except exact OCCURED_COMMUNICATIN_ERROR, which opens the utility-targeted warning.

S001/S002/S003 Exit -> detached confirmation callback. Confirmed S001 exits immediately; confirmed S002/S003 performs forced communication/session setup, normal mode and communication termination before routing. S004–S007 Exit emits backToUtilityMenu immediately.
Exact branch-specific status routes, unknown-status behavior, callback ordering and cleanup are retained in member_contracts.

request_construction.worker_transport: Csn11WorkerApi returns GtsWorkerApi.send promises unchanged. The exact command table and argument omission are retained in member_contracts and semantic_constants.
request_construction.dispatch_envelope: Worker initialization/selection/bumper handlers consume param.parameter with {ecuId}, {checked} or {bumperType}. Envelope construction remains a shared-owner responsibility.
request_construction.platform: startGeneralComm({ecuId,busId}); setNegativeResponseCondition({repReqRetryMax:0}); transitSession({modeId:1}) or ({modeId:3}); endGeneralComm() without arguments.
request_construction.utility: Every local utility send uses {reqType:0,reqBody} with ordinary JavaScript arrays. Exact byte arrays and concat formulas are specified per worker method.
request_construction.support: parsePhase5Support receives the entire {isSuccess:true,resBody} adapter result; isSupport(...did) filters [0x1c,0x04..0x07] and [0x1b,0x01..0x0c] without reordering.
request_construction.logging: ActivityLogger receives the exact title/text/list payloads documented in controller method entries. No logging return values are consumed.

response_error_mapping.adapter: sendMessage returns {isSuccess:true,resBody:result.apiArgs.resBody} or {isSuccess:false}; boolean sends accept any fulfillment and return false on throw/rejection. No local native result-code, SID or body validation occurs in these adapters.
response_error_mapping.platform: Nonforced checked platform operations require resultInfo.result === 0; catch(e=>e) does not protect subsequent field access from malformed rejection values.
response_error_mapping.statuses: SUCCESS, FAILED_SEND_MESSAGE, OCCURED_COMMUNICATIN_ERROR, OCCURED_COMMUNICATIN_ERROR_S001, ENTERING_BUMPER_TYPE, EXPLANATION_INITIALIZATION, RETYPE_BUMPER_TYPE, FAILURE_TO_MEET_THE_INITIALIZATION_CONDITIONS, FAILURE_INITIALIZATION, CONDITIONS_NOT_MET_OR_MALFUNCTION and BACK_TO_UTILITY retain their exact spellings and per-method routes.
response_error_mapping.conversion: Phase-1 failure bytes become an Error Factor string. Phase-2 raw bus and sensor records become ordered display rows. Sparse tables, falsy fallbacks, model/view differences and malformed-input exceptions remain as documented per conversion method.
response_error_mapping.frontend_recovery: FAILED_SEND_MESSAGE awaits inherited showCommErrorDialog then returns to S001. Communication-warning routes distinguish S001 and utility. Unknown statuses and uncaught failures have no blanket recovery.

user_visible_result.title: ECU Calibration
user_visible_result.screens: S001 selects parts; S002 enters Bumper Type; S003 explains sensor initialization; S004 displays initialization-condition failure with Try Again; S005 displays bus failure factors; S006 displays bus factors and per-sensor write-protect/match/memorized-ID states; S007 reports completion.
user_visible_result.completion: The success report text is 'This utility is successful'. S007 says data will not display until connection is reestablished and information updates only after vehicle reconnection; no reconnection is performed locally.
user_visible_result.warnings: DL003 instructs engine/power OFF then ON with Engine OFF/Ready OFF and acknowledgment; the source does not measure those actions. Exit confirmation retains the mismatched Vehicle Information Registration Utility wording.
user_visible_result.resource_authority: All referenced non-null resource IDs have supplied English labels. Exact supplied values are retained in semantic_constants.resource_labels.

mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.communication: Cleanup is branch-specific, not a finally. communicationTerminationProcess and callCommonEndSendMessage request session 1 then endGeneralComm without normal mode. callCommonEndProcessSuccessOrNot requests normal mode, session 1 and endGeneralComm, returning only the normal-mode boolean.
mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.cancel: Phase 1 resets cancelFlag=false. changeCancelFlag sets it true without interrupting a pending wait/request. Phase 2 checks it only at the outer loop boundary; an iteration returning a result wins over a flag change within that iteration.
mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.dialogs: Only modalView is explicitly tracked/closed. Confirmation/warning dialogs use detached buttonPressed.then callbacks. Repeated confirmations overwrite dl006BtnPressed; unrecognized confirmation IDs leave its deferred unresolved.
mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.disposal: Controller dispose calls current view.disposeView() then eventDisp.dispose(), with no await, null guard, model/worker disposal, dialog closure, communication termination or cancel mutation.
mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.exceptions: There is no local blanket catch/finally, global rejection recovery, timeout, worker teardown or automatic model cleanup. Precise exceptions to this statement are the local send adapters and platform promise catch(e=>e) calls documented below.

business_sequence: This unit presents ECU Calibration for the Clearance Warning ECU and ultrasonic sensors. Its first screen instructs the operator to keep the engine/power switch ON with Engine OFF/Ready OFF, stop the vehicle, select replaced or removed parts, and not turn IG OFF after Next. These are displayed instructions, not measured admission conditions in this source.

Controller initialization creates the model, dialog owner, and screen factory, initializes display resources, sends worker initialization with {ecuId: commonInfo.getCurrentEcuId()} without awaiting it, resets screen/selection/cancellation-dialog state, logs the ECU Calibration title, and displays S001.

S001 enables Next when any of its three checkboxes is checked. The controller retains and reports all three selection records, but sends only customEvent.args[1][0].value as {checked}. Thus selection of the Clearance Warning ECU, not the overall presence of any selection, chooses whether vehicle-specification registration and bumper-type entry are requested.

The worker starts general communication, sets repReqRetryMax to 0, requests session 1 then session 3, and sends the dealer-mode request. With checked truthy it also requests the store-vehicle-specification routine. Successful S001 paths terminate communication through session 1 and endGeneralComm, then return ENTERING_BUMPER_TYPE or EXPLANATION_INITIALIZATION.

S002 accepts up to two ASCII/full-width decimal digits through DOM filtering. Its controller passes the current textbox value unchanged as {bumperType}; the worker applies parseInt(value,10), reads the maximum bumper type, compares against its low nibble, writes an admitted value, reads it back, and requires strict byte equality. Out-of-range returns RETYPE_BUMPER_TYPE without immediate communication termination; acknowledging its warning explicitly invokes callCommonEndSendMessage before showing S002 again.

S003 explains ultrasonic sensor initialization and asks the operator to verify sensor angle/height against the repair manual. Phase 1 resets cancelFlag, starts communication and session 3, and sends the initialization request. A failed request triggers a read of initialization-condition failure factors. Nonzero returned factors are displayed on S004 after normal-mode/communication cleanup; Try Again returns to S003 without starting another request until Next is pressed.

Successful phase 1 leaves communication active, replaces the initial wait dialog with a cancellable processing dialog, and starts phase 2. Phase 2 repeatedly waits 200 milliseconds and reads initialization status. It accepts all first-four masked status values equal to 1 as success, repeats while those values are not all in {1,2}, and otherwise obtains supported bus failure-factor DIDs in deterministic order.

A completed/failed result reads supported 1C04 through 1C07. An empty supported list, malformed/failed reads, or a list consisting entirely of 0 or entirely of 1 routes to failed-send cleanup. Write-protect-condition or malfunction values trigger optional reads of supported 1B01 through 1B0C. Results become S005 bus-error rows or S006 bus-error plus per-sensor state rows; the frontend converts bytes through resource lookup tables and logs the same displayed rows.

Cancel on the processing dialog opens confirmation and stores a deferred promise. Yes shows the noncancellable wait dialog, sends changeCancelFlag without awaiting it, and resolves the deferred as 'Yes'. No reopens the processing dialog and resolves it as 'No'. The worker observes cancellation only at the phase-2 while-loop boundary, then attempts normal mode, session 1, and endGeneralComm. After phase 2 resolves, the controller additionally waits for any currently stored confirmation promise before choosing its final route.

Successful initialization logs 'This utility is successful' and shows S007, whose text says data will not display/update until vehicle reconnection. Failure and communication-error paths retain the exact distinct status spellings and routes described below. The communication warning instructs the operator to power OFF then ON and acknowledge; the source does not verify those operations.

Exit from S001, S002, or S003 asks the confirmation text 'Do you want to exit the Vehicle Information Registration Utility?' despite this unit being titled ECU Calibration. Confirmed S001 exit immediately emits backToUtilityMenu; S002/S003 first use forced communication/session setup, normal-mode request, and communication termination. S004–S007 Exit immediately emit that event.

There are no local try/finally blocks, global rejection recovery, interval handles, timeout cancellation, worker teardown, or automatic model cleanup on controller disposal. Only the send-message adapters catch all request failures and return booleans/objects; platform wrappers use catch(e=>e) and then may still fail when expected resultInfo fields are absent. This contract describes source behavior, not execution or verified ECU effects.

methods.semantics: Returns (await callCommonEndProcessSuccessOrNot()) ? {status:'FAILED_SEND_MESSAGE'} : {status:'OCCURED_COMMUNICATIN_ERROR'}.

methods.semantics: Awaits transitSessionMode1(), then endGeneralComm(); returns {status:'OCCURED_COMMUNICATIN_ERROR_S001'}.

methods.semantics: Inside try, awaits gts.util.SendMessageForUtility({reqType,reqBody}); returns {isSuccess:true,resBody:result.apiArgs.resBody}. catch without a binding returns {isSuccess:false}.
branches: Any rejection or synchronous error inside try, including accessing a missing apiArgs, becomes isSuccess:false. A present apiArgs with undefined resBody can still return isSuccess:true.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: No native result code, response SID, length, or bytes are checked here. No finally or communication cleanup.

branches: Any fulfilled result is accepted without inspecting any fields; any throw/rejection returns false.

semantic_constants.source_offset_convention: Offsets are raw source character offsets with an exclusive end. Defining-region anchors below include each complete constant definition; resolved values come directly from supplied authoritative definitions and labels. No execution is asserted.

controller.semantics: BACK_TO_UTILITY_MENU is emitted without payload. Dl006Btn values resolve and select the cancellation-confirmation override. semantics.SENSOR_BUS: Fr, Rr, FrSide and RrSide define the four display bus labels, indexed by DID low byte 4 through 7 after four leading null entries.
semantics.ERROR_FACTOR: All named scalar IDs, per-bus NotInstalled IDs and ordered $1C04/$1C05/$1C06/$1C07 arrays are defined in the linked complete mapping. initializeResources builds the exact sparse S004 and indexed S005 tables retained in its method entry.
semantics.SENSOR_NAME: The twelve IDs define the ascending 1B01–1B0C display sensor order.
semantics.MEMORIZED_SENSOR_ID_STATE: All nineteen ID keys are defined in the linked complete mapping. Twelve sensor-specific rows retain positional annotations for ID1, ID2, ID3, ID4, ID5 and ID6 exactly as initialized.
semantics.MATCH_STATUS: Indices 0,1,2 resolve to Undetermined, Mismatched, Matched.

worker_api_commands.semantics: Each value is sent unchanged and matches its worker commandHandler key. INIT, PRESS_S001_NEXT_BUTTON and PRESS_S002_NEXT_BUTTON supply a second argument; all remaining wrappers omit it. The last command deliberately omits call in the command string.

worker_local_constants.semantics: LIMIT_BUMPER_TYPE is the low nibble of result1.resBody.slice(3)[0]; the parsed bumperType is admitted by <= only. LIMIT_BUMPER_TYPE itself is runtime-derived.
The failed initialization-request factor read requires three header bytes plus one payload byte.
Support/read admission lengths and ordered candidate DID arrays are exact. Runtime support filtering retains candidate order and sequential reads retain that order.
A fresh frozen status object is created per call. Completed-only inspects at most four payload bytes after masking; empty input passes every.
A separate fresh frozen object is created per call. Completed-and-failed-only admits each masked value 1 or 2, including all-completed and empty input.
The exact write-protect-condition Map is retained in existNotMetWriteProtectProcessCondition: byte position 0, mask 255, low DID 4/5 -> 14 and 6/7 -> 10.
The exact malfunction Map is retained in existUltrasonicSensorMalfunction: byte position 0, mask 255, low DID 4/5 -> [10,11,12,13] and 6/7 -> [8,9].

frontend_local_constants.semantics: MAX_LENGTH truncates the filtered digit string. Conversion subtracts 0xFEE0 from full-width digit character codes; exact composition/input/change ordering is retained in the screen method.
Twelve closures per state category use these exact payload byte positions and mask; falsy lookup results use r_item_i6100.

S004 parsing masks the first byte and applies a falsy fallback. Bus conversion tests the unmasked first byte against 15, then masks for table indexing; its fallback/throw distinctions are retained per method.

resource_binding.presentation_source: Unit view/dialog methods construct inline DOM or supply typed content/button/table parameters to shared UtilityView/createCommonDialog; no external workflow HTML template path is referenced by these members. Exact inline HTML and options are preserved in source evidence.

shared_framework.semantics: Shared base controllers, views, models, UtilityView events and rendering, common dialogs, and EventDispatcher are cross-owner dependencies, not missing local sources. gts.common runtime and native services likewise have separate owners. The typed handoffs below describe this utility's calls without inventing those owners' internals.
shared_framework.event_type_rule: Shared EventDispatcher permits undefined event types. Registration and triggering with undefined address the same coerced property; an undefined event value alone does not prevent delivery. Event values are not an admission or delivery failure predicate in this contract.

entry_admission.programmatic: Construction accepts commonInfo. init establishes model/view/dialog objects, initializes the worker for commonInfo.getCurrentEcuId(), starts communication, and requires all documented A115/A125 support bits. Optional A125 bit 3 controls position-registration UI availability, not overall utility admission.
entry_admission.displayed_instructions: Engine/power switch ON with Engine OFF/Ready OFF, registered transmitter IDs before position-only registration, and avoiding the Tire Pressure Monitor System switch are displayed instructions, not tested vehicle predicates.
entry_admission.operation_specific: ID/Tire Number Registration remains selectable independently of position support. Combined and position-only controls are disabled for falsy position support, but cached choices and controller events are not independently revalidated. Set2 admission performs the documented four-ID all-zero Set1 check.

input_domain.controller_events: evt.args[1] contains ordered objects with value properties for useParam screens; handlers access the structure without guards. Radio values are exact case-sensitive strings. Position-only Next reads the DOM rather than an event parameter array.
input_domain.registration_data: Worker reads expose four-byte ID slices, wheel counts 4/5, tire-set encodings 0/3, and masked location codes. ID-entry UI admits eight-character strings after the documented hexadecimal normalization and length test; it does not reject zero or duplicate IDs.
input_domain.worker_envelope: Bound worker handlers receive model as their first argument and a second argument with parameter containing the exact model-layer parameter object.

state_fields.controller: commonInfo; eventDisp; activityReport; model, cmnView, cmnDlg, view; currentTireSetChangeFlag=0; currentNumberOfTiresChangeFlag=0; prevScreen=null; tirePositionRegistration=false; numberOfWheel=null; tireSet=null; idCode={}; location=null; selectTireSet=null; writeData={}; select={stpw15002:'',stpw15003:'',stpw15004:'',stpw15005:'',stpw15008:''}.
state_fields.view_factory: input={stpw15002:null,stpw15003:null,stpw15004:null,stpw15005:null,stpw15006:{},stpw15007:{},stpw15008:null,stpw15009:{},stpw15012:{}}; screen objects are distinct from this persistent factory/cache.
state_fields.dialog: eventDisp and dlg=null; only the wait dialog is retained in dlg.
state_fields.worker: commandHandler={}, buffer=null, commonInfo=null, ecuCache=null, cache=null, commandThread=null, storedCache=null. initTpw15 replaces cache with {data:{ecuInfo,numberOfWheel:null,tireSet:null}}. writeIdCode can add cache.data.reqBody2503 containing the original full response.

guarded_ordered_transitions.initialization: See Tpw15Controller.prototype.init and business_sequence[1]: initial screen → wait → worker cache initialization → start → support reads/check → stop → operation selection; initialization error cleanup → communication error → menu event.
guarded_ordered_transitions.registration: See operation handlers in member_contracts and business_sequence[2] through business_sequence[10]: operation selection → current wheel/set read → position-only selection or spare/set/entry route → logged confirmation → ordered write transaction → completion.
guarded_ordered_transitions.control_rejections: onClickSTpw15005ViewNextBtn deliberately rejects with showScreenFunc for the Set1-required notice or current-set-change screen; its catch returns that function without communication-error cleanup.
guarded_ordered_transitions.promise_order: Every controller/worker chain described in member_contracts retains its returned nested promises. Event registration and DOM listener installation do not return transaction promises to the registering method. No transaction is serialized or canceled by disposal.

request_construction.model_and_transport: Exact model parameter objects and command strings are in Tpw15Model and Tpw15WorkerApi method entries. stopComm always wraps its argument in {defaultSession:argument}, including the screen-004 object argument.
request_construction.ecu_requests: Exact read/write arrays, bit expressions, response-body cloning, suffix substring parsing, and ordered optional flag operations are specified in the Tpw15WorkerModel method entries.
request_construction.logging_and_rendering: Exact retainedData layouts, resource keys, screen templates, button parameters, and ordering are preserved in controller/view/dialog entries.

response_error_mapping.controller: Response.result is tested by truthiness. Start failure normally rejects {defaultSession:false}; data/write failures reject {defaultSession:true}. The later start in screen 005 instead rejects {defaultSession:true}. Catch cleanup awaits stop before closing wait and awaiting communication-error UI; cleanup failures are not recaught by the same catch.
response_error_mapping.worker: Send helpers require response.resultInfo.result === 0. Read decoders additionally enforce their documented minimum lengths and masks. Most command chains map failure to resolved {result:false}, retaining documented partial outputs. Synchronous setup before the chain can throw outside its catch. stopComm swallows ordinary native transition/end promise rejections and returns true without establishing native success.
response_error_mapping.special_cases: Negative-response-condition setup ignores both fulfillment fields and rejection. ID main-send rejection can attempt written-flag restoration before reporting false. Combined location failure optionally awaits writeWrittenFlag, ignores its resolved result fields, then deliberately enters the controller error path.

user_visible_result.screens: Operation selection, spare-transmitter configuration, tire-count choice, tire-set choice/current-set change, plain/spatial ID entry, position dropdowns, write confirmations, and selected-operation completion.
user_visible_result.dialogs: Please wait.; spare-change Yes/No warning; utility-exit Yes/No confirmation; Set1-registration-required OK notice; inherited communication-error dialog.
user_visible_result.success: Only after the transaction's stop resolves does the controller log 'This utility is successful', close wait, and display the selected operation followed by 'is completed.'. Completion Exit emits backToUtilityMenu directly.

mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.mutation: Selections, flags, read assignments, entry caches, and written-flag response cache mutate at the precise points documented below; later failures do not generally roll them back. Successful writes do not refresh controller wheel/set state or worker wheel/set cache.
mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.cleanup: Screen replacement conditionally disposes the prior screen. Controller dispose disposes only the current view and its own dispatcher. Wait close affects only the retained wait dialog.
mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.cancel: No cancellation token, in-flight-dispose guard, transaction serialization, timer, retry loop, or local communication stop on exit/menu emission/dispose. Written-flag restoration is a narrowly scoped attempted write, not a general rollback guarantee.

business_sequence: This is a source-derived contract, not an execution report. The utility registers transmitter IDs, the number of tires with transmitters, and optionally tire positions. The supplied English instructions require engine/power ON with engine/Ready OFF, advise ID/Tire Number Registration for tires not immediately installed, require registered IDs before position-only registration, and say not to operate the tire-pressure-monitor-system switch while working. These instructions are displayed text, not programmatically tested vehicle conditions.

Construction establishes controller state and inherited base prototypes. Initialization creates the model, reusable view factory/input cache, and dialog factory; logs the utility title; shows an empty initial screen; opens Please wait; initializes the worker cache using the current ECU ID; starts communication; checks required DID-support bits; stops communication with a default-session request; closes Please wait; and shows operation selection. A failed initialization chain attempts stopComm(reason.defaultSession), closes the wait dialog, shows the inherited communication-error dialog, and only after that resolves triggers return to the utility menu.

Operation selection admits ID/Tire Number Registration independently of position support. If the returned tirePositionRegistration value is falsy, the combined-registration and position-only radio controls are disabled. A remembered radio DOM ID can nevertheless be restored without checking its disabled state. Next is initially disabled only when there is no remembered selection. The controller does not independently validate an event against disabled controls.

Next reads the wheel count and current tire set. Position-only registration additionally reads the current set's four or five IDs and location mapping, then proceeds directly to position selection. Other operations reset both change flags and proceed to the spare-transmitter configuration question.

Choosing Change for spare configuration opens confirmation explaining that registration will use Set1 and Set2 cannot be selected again until its IDs are registered again. Yes sets currentNumberOfTiresChangeFlag=1 and opens the four/five-tire choice; No sets the flag to zero and proceeds to tire-set selection. Not choosing Change bypasses that dialog and sets the flag to zero. The four/five-tire screen disables the currently active configuration and requires a selection unless one is cached.

Changing the wheel configuration selects Set1 unconditionally, sets currentTireSetChangeFlag according to whether the current set is Set2, reads Set1 IDs for the newly selected tire count, optionally reads locations, and opens either plain ID entry or spatial ID entry. The successful stop call here deliberately passes {defaultSession:true} as the argument to a method that wraps it in another defaultSession field.

Tire-set selection maps Set1 to 0x00 and all other selection strings to 0x03. Selecting the literal Set2 first reads Set1's four IDs; if all returned bytes are zero, communication is stopped and the informational Set1-registration-required dialog is shown, leaving the existing set-selection screen in place. Selecting the set opposite the current set instead routes through the current-set-change question after closing the wait dialog.

The current-set-change screen forces Change and disables Don't Change when the cached operation DOM ID is radio002_1. Otherwise the user must select or restore a cached choice. The controller turns only the literal Change into flag 1. Entry reads use Set1 whenever the selected set is Set1 or the number-of-tires change flag is 1; otherwise they use Set2. Plain and spatial entry preserve their own cached input values across recreation.

ID entry displays four-byte big-endian values as eight uppercase hexadecimal characters and blanks all-zero values. During non-composing input and compositionend, fullwidth ASCII letters/digits are converted, non-hex characters removed, and remaining text uppercased. Next is disabled whenever any document input has length other than eight. This is not a uniqueness or nonzero-ID test. Plain entry uses document input order directly; spatial entry remaps its DOM order FL, RL, FR, RR, optional Spare into id1=FL, id2=FR, id3=RL, id4=RR, id5=Spare.

Entry Next constructs writeData and logs a retained list before displaying a write-confirmation screen. ID-only Write starts communication, optionally clears the stored written flag when the tire-count change flag is 1, sends the ID-registration body, stops communication, logs This utility is successful, closes Please wait, and shows completion. Combined Write performs the same ID write and then writes canonical locations 1,2,3,4 and optionally 5. If the location result is falsy and the tire-count-change flag is 1, it attempts writeWrittenFlag before deliberately entering the communication-error path.

Position-only entry maps registered IDs into per-position dropdowns, marks duplicate mappings as unselected, and requires complete unique dropdown values through a uniqueness test that includes an initial empty-string sentinel. Duplicate nonempty values have red backgrounds. Next gathers document-wide selects, sorts their label-plus-hex strings lexically, logs the resulting ID/position rows, and displays confirmation. Write uses the sorted array positions as id1 through id5 and writes only location data; transmitter IDs themselves are not sent in this operation.

Most read/write controller transactions use Promise.resolve().then chains, not await syntax, try/finally, polling, or timers. Start-result failures ordinarily reject {defaultSession:false}; data/result failures reject {defaultSession:true}. The later start in the tire-set-selection path instead rejects {defaultSession:true}. Each specified catch awaits stopComm before closing the wait dialog and showing errors. A rejection in cleanup or in a catch's own chain is not caught again by that same catch. There is no cancellation token, transaction serialization, timer, retry loop, or in-flight-dispose guard in this unit.

Exit on working screens opens an auto-closing Yes/No confirmation; only Yes emits backToUtilityMenu. Completion Exit emits that event immediately. Controller disposal disposes the current view and its own event dispatcher but neither stops communication nor disposes the model, common view factory, dialog factory, or worker. Worker commands and native/common-runtime calls are handoffs with the exact source-level predicates described below; no additional ECU protocol meaning or native behavior is asserted.

member_contracts.semantics: The supplied member record has relevant_definitions=[]. Shared UtilityView.ViewEvent definitions are framework-owned at diagnostic_operations.frontend_contracts.MenuShell; local controller events and worker commands have explicit semantic entries below. semantics: Initial locals tirePositionRegistration=false, supportA115={}, supportA125={}.

First then sends [0x22,0xA1,0x15]. Requires resBody.length >= 9. Assigns supportA115={did1525:resBody[7] >> 2 & 0x01,did1526:resBody[7] >> 1 & 0x01,did1527:resBody[7] >> 0 & 0x01,did1528:resBody[8] >> 7 & 0x01,did1529:resBody[8] >> 6 & 0x01,did152A:resBody[8] >> 5 & 0x01,did152B:resBody[8] >> 4 & 0x01,did152C:resBody[8] >> 3 & 0x01,did152D:resBody[8] >> 2 & 0x01,did152E:resBody[8] >> 1 & 0x01}.

Next sends [0x22,0xA1,0x25]. Requires resBody.length >= 4. Assigns supportA125={did2500:resBody[3] >> 7 & 0x01,did2501:resBody[3] >> 6 & 0x01,did2502:resBody[3] >> 5 & 0x01}; tirePositionRegistration=Boolean(resBody[3] >> 3 & 0x01).
Next rejects if Object.values(supportA115).some(did=>did === 0) || Object.values(supportA125).some(did=>did === 0). Then returns createReturnValue(true); catch returns createReturnValue(false).

Nested sendMessage(reqBody) calls gts.util.SendMessageForUtility({reqType:0,reqBody:reqBody}); fulfillment resolves response only if response.resultInfo.result === 0, otherwise rejects. Native rejection propagates to enclosing catch.

semantics: Reads cacheData=model.cache.data before chain. Sends [0x22,0x25,0x00]; requires resBody.length >= 4; assigns cacheData.numberOfWheel=resBody[3] & 0x07; rejects unless exactly 0x04 or 0x05.
Then sends [0x22,0x25,0x02]; requires length >= 4; assigns cacheData.tireSet=resBody[3] & 0x03; rejects unless exactly 0x00 or 0x03.
Then createReturnValue(true); catch createReturnValue(false). Nested sendMessage calls SendMessageForUtility({reqType:0,reqBody}) and requires response.resultInfo.result === 0 to resolve response.

methods.branches: Invalid decoded values are assigned before validation and remain in cache and returned failure data. First-read failure skips second read.

semantics: Starts idCode={}. Each response callback rejects when apiArgs.resBody.length < 7, otherwise assigns idCode.idN=response.apiArgs.resBody.slice(3,7).
If param.parameter.readId5 is truthy, a fifth sequential step sends Set1 [0x22,0x15,0x29] versus Set2 [0x22,0x15,0x2E] and applies same length and slice rule.

Then returns createReturnValue(true); catch returns createReturnValue(false). Nested sendMessage uses SendMessageForUtility({reqType:0,reqBody}) and strictly requires response.resultInfo.result === 0.
Nested createReturnValue returns Promise.resolve({result:result,idCode:idCode}).
methods.branches: readId5 uses truthiness; tireSet uses strict equality. First failure stops subsequent reads.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: Failure returns already accumulated ID fields; no ECU cache mutation or echo validation.

methods.semantics: Starts location={}; resolved chain sends [0x22,0x25,0x04]. Callback rejects if resBody.length < 8; else assigns location.id1=resBody[3]&0x07,id2=resBody[4]&0x07,id3=resBody[5]&0x07,id4=resBody[6]&0x07,id5=resBody[7]&0x07. methods.branches: Always decodes five location values even for four tires; does not validate 1..5 or uniqueness.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: No cache mutation or protocol echo checks.

semantics: Reads cacheData=model.cache.data before chain. First then runs only if param.parameter.currentNumberOfTiresChangeFlag === 1: sends [0x22,0x25,0x03], requires response.apiArgs.resBody.length >= 5, copies entire response body into cacheData.reqBody2503=[...response.apiArgs.resBody], clones it into reqBody2503, sets reqBody2503[0]=0x2E and reqBody2503[4]=reqBody2503[4] & 0x7F, and returns sendMessage(reqBody2503).

Next sets currentTireSetChangeFlag=param.parameter.currentTireSetChangeFlag === 1?0x10:0x00; tireSet=param.parameter.tireSet === 0x03?0x08:0x00; id1..id4 from param.parameter.idCode; id5=param.parameter.idCode.id5 ?? '00000000'.

Builds exact 24-element request [0x2E,0x25,0x01,currentTireSetChangeFlag | tireSet | param.parameter.numberOfWheel,parseInt(id1.substring(id1.length-8,id1.length-6),16),parseInt(id1.substring(id1.length-6,id1.length-4),16),parseInt(id1.substring(id1.length-4,id1.length-2),16),parseInt(id1.substring(id1.length-2,id1.length-0),16),parseInt(id2.substring(id2.length-8,id2.length-6),16),parseInt(id2.substring(id2.length-6,id2.length-4),16),parseInt(id2.substring(id2.length-4,id2.length-2),16),parseInt(id2.substring(id2.length-2,id2.length-0),16),parseInt(id3.substring(id3.length-8,id3.length-6),16),parseInt(id3.substring(id3.length-6,id3.length-4),16),parseInt(id3.substring(id3.length-4,id3.length-2),16),parseInt(id3.substring(id3.length-2,id3.length-0),16),parseInt(id4.substring(id4.length-8,id4.length-6),16),parseInt(id4.substring(id4.length-6,id4.length-4),16),parseInt(id4.substring(id4.length-4,id4.length-2),16),parseInt(id4.substring(id4.length-2,id4.length-0),16),parseInt(id5.substring(id5.length-8,id5.length-6),16),parseInt(id5.substring(id5.length-6,id5.length-4),16),parseInt(id5.substring(id5.length-4,id5.length-2),16),parseInt(id5.substring(id5.length-2,id5.length-0),16)].

Returns sendMessage(reqBody).catch: if currentNumberOfTiresChangeFlag === 1, clones cacheData.reqBody2503, sets byte 0 to 0x2E and byte 4 to byte4 | 0x80, sends it, and on successful resolution deliberately Promise.reject(); otherwise directly Promise.reject(). Restoration rejection also propagates.

Outer then returns createReturnValue(true); outer catch returns createReturnValue(false). Nested sendMessage calls SendMessageForUtility({reqType:0,reqBody:reqBody}) and requires response.resultInfo.result === 0; createReturnValue returns Promise.resolve({result:result}).
methods.branches: Restoration applies only to rejection of main sendMessage promise, not failure of earlier flag-read/clear step or an exception constructing main body. Flags use strict ===1. Set2 uses strict ===0x03. Missing/null id5 uses four zero bytes; empty string is not replaced. No explicit byte validation or NaN rejection. methods.effects_and_cleanup: Stores original full 2503 response, not modified clear request. Does not update wheel/tire cache after writing. Restoration sets bit 7 rather than restoring its original bit value; no rollback guarantee.

methods.branches: No length, range, uniqueness, response-body, or echo validation.

resource_binding.presentation_source: Unit view/dialog methods construct inline DOM or supply typed content/button/table parameters to shared UtilityView/createCommonDialog; no external workflow HTML template path is referenced by these members. Exact inline HTML and options are preserved in source evidence.

entry_admission.initialization: Rlp01Controller.init(initArgs) ignores initArgs, constructs the model/view/dialog factories, initializes def=null and isAborted=false, logs the title, and initializes the worker with commonInfo.getCurrentEcuId() before displaying the introductory screen.
entry_admission.next: NEXT_BTN invokes onClickSRlp01001ViewNextBtn. The displayed vehicle preparation conditions are instructions, not machine-enforced guards. There is no running flag, admission lock, button disabling or reentrancy guard.
entry_admission.worker_registration: The entire worker definition and final instance registration execute only if !workerController.workerModels['Rlp01']. A truthy existing entry skips that block.
entry_admission.shared_framework: Shared framework behavior is available cross-owner at diagnostic_operations.frontend_contracts.MenuShell. gts.common runtime and native-facing implementations are separate owners, not missing local sources.

input_domain.controller: commonInfo; unused initArgs; view events; dialog buttonPressed fulfillment objects whose id is compared strictly with 'Cancel', 'Yes' or 'No'.
input_domain.worker_envelope: initRlp01 reads param.parameter.ecuId; setIsAborted reads param.parameter.isAborted. Other operation handlers ignore param. Envelope construction and dispatch belong to the shared runtime owner.
input_domain.communication: Start consumes response.apiArgs.resBody.length. Check additionally consumes resBody[5] via JavaScript bitwise & 0xFF, and rejection response?.errorCode and response?.detailCode. No local strict byte-array validation or response-prefix validation exists.
input_domain.runtime_values: Concrete ECU selection/lookup, user timing, transport scheduling, backend/native fulfillment and rejection values are runtime_inputs.

controller.cmnView: Initially null; assigned Rlp01View in init.
controller.cmnDlg: Initially null; assigned Rlp01Dialog in init.
controller.currentView: Initially null; assigned the direct return from createRlp01001/createRlp01002.
controller.modalView: Initially null; assigned only the noncancelable loader return by showSRlp01Dl001; not cleared by closeLoaderDialog.
controller.def: Initialized null; replaced by a new deferred on each recognized Cancel. Never reset to null after confirmation.
controller.isAborted: Initialized false; reset false before Next's worker propagation; set true after showing DL001 on cancel-confirmation Yes.

dialog.loaderDlg: Not explicitly initialized by the constructor. DL001/DL002 lazily cache and reuse it; closeLoaderDialog closes a truthy value then assigns null.

worker_api.api: New GtsWorkerApi(commonInfo); commonInfo is undefined on the model construction path.

worker.commandHandler: Initially {}; six command keys installed by initCommandHandler.
worker.buffer: Initially null; no subsequent local use.
worker.cache: Initially null; replaced by initRlp01 with {data:{ecuInfo:{ecuId,busId},isAborted:false}}.
worker.storedCache: Initially null; no subsequent local use.
worker.polling_locals: errorStatus initially COMERROR=2; isloopContinueStatus=true; isNegativeRes=false; resdetailCode=0. Negative-response flags are assigned by the send-helper catch and are not reset by subsequent successful responses.

guarded_ordered_transitions.order: Construct factories and flags; log title; await initRlp01 through the returned chain; show introductory screen. Chain rejection goes to inherited onErrorCommon as a direct, unbound catch callback.

Set controller.isAborted=false; await model.setIsAborted(false); show DL001; await setup; await start routine; close loader; launch DL002 without adopting its promise; await gated polling interpretation.

startGeneralComm({ecuId,busId}); setNegativeResponseCondition({repReqRetryMax:0}); transitSession({modeId:1}); transitSession({modeId:3}). Negative-response-setting promise rejection is swallowed. Other awaited setup failure attempts awaited endGeneralComm and rejects {}.

If cacheData.isAborted is truthy, resolve current status immediately without worker cleanup. Otherwise await wait(200), send check, await default-session attempt, await communication-close attempt, then resolve status 0 or reject status 1/2. A VC000003 rejection with NRC21/NRC24 instead repeats, including another wait(200), without terminal cleanup.

Replace def; close loader; launch DL003 detached. DL003 Yes shows DL001, sets controller abort true, awaits worker flag propagation, then resolves def. No launches DL002 detached then resolves def. Unknown DL003 id does not resolve the gate.

Controller abort true takes priority over result status on both fulfillment and rejection: await explicit worker default-session/close operation, close loader, emit menu navigation without adopting navigation's promise. Otherwise fulfillment logs success and replaces the screen; rejection status 1 shows DL005, while status 2/default shows inherited communication error.

request_construction.ecu_cache: Copy only ecuInfo.ecuId and ecuInfo.busId from getEcuInfoByEcuId(param.parameter.ecuId).
request_construction.types: The message bodies are ordinary JavaScript arrays. Payloads are JavaScript objects; no local typed-array conversion or native ABI schema is introduced. Exact call order and exception handling remain in the worker method contracts.

response_error_mapping.start: Reject when resBody.length < 5; otherwise accept without testing response prefix or status. Response callback access failures also enter the helper's rejection path. Ordinary operation failure becomes rejection {} after an awaited default-session attempt and detached communication-close attempt.

check.other_error: Attempt ordered default-session/communication-close cleanup, assign COMERROR=2, reject {result:{comResult:2}}.
check.abort_at_entry: Fulfill current errorStatus, initially 2, without worker cleanup.

response_error_mapping.controller: Initial setIsAborted(false) rejection is outside the later local catch chain. Setup rejection normally maps to inherited communication error; start rejection normally maps to DL005. Check interpretation first tests controller.isAborted, then uses status 1 for DL005 and status 2/default for inherited communication error. Nested catches also cover callback failures; malformed check rejection lacking result.result can throw and flow to the start catch. See the full Next method contract for exact adoption and detached-dialog behavior.

mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.polling: No independent timer handle, timeout, attempt limit, total deadline or explicit timer clear exists locally. Abort is only checked at iteration entry and does not independently interrupt wait/request.
mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.gate: def gates controller interpretation of either polling fulfillment or rejection, not the worker operation. It is never reset to null; subsequent Cancel replaces it. Unknown confirmation ids or failed worker abort propagation can leave the gate unresolved.
mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.worker_cleanup: Terminal check outcomes and nonretry check errors await default-session then communication-close attempts. Retry and entry-abort paths skip that worker cleanup. Setup failure awaits close only. Start failure awaits default-session then launches close detached. Explicit transitDefaultSession awaits default-session then close and does not reset isAborted.
mutation_cleanup_cancel_semantics.controller_cleanup: Abort interpretation explicitly requests cleanup and then closes the loader and navigates. dispose only disposes currentView and the controller dispatcher; it does not abort polling, close dialogs, resolve def, dispose model, or clean up native communication.

business_sequence: The constants section conditionally declares an empty Rlp01 function when Rlp01 === undefined. Rlp01.ERROR_STATUS is frozen with ERROR_NONE:0, INIT_FAIL:1 and COMERROR:2. gts.ERROR_CODE.NEGATIVE_RESPONSE is 'VC000003'; retry detail constants BUSY_REPEAT_REQUEST and REQUEST_SEQUENCE_ERROR are 'NRC21' and 'NRC24'.

Initialization constructs the model, view factory and dialog factory, sets def=null and isAborted=false, logs the title 'Height Sensor Initialization', initializes the worker cache for commonInfo.getCurrentEcuId(), and then shows the introductory screen. Initialization rejection is passed to inherited onErrorCommon.

The introductory screen describes engine/power ON with Engine OFF/Ready OFF, an empty passenger compartment, an empty trunk except the spare tire and attached tools, a flat vehicle surface, correct Height Sensor connection, and prior completion of 'Switch Specification Information'. These are instructions only: no local code validates these conditions or prevents Next based on them.

Next resets the controller abort flag and awaits propagation of false to the worker before showing the noncancelable 'Please wait.' loader. It starts general communication, attempts to disable negative-response retries using repReqRetryMax:0, enters modeId:1 and then modeId:3. A rejected negative-response-condition operation is deliberately ignored; other setup failures attempt to end communication and reject.

The start request is {reqType:0,reqBody:[49,1,17,3]}. Only response.apiArgs.resBody.length >= 5 is required locally; no response prefix or status byte is checked. Start failure attempts default-session transition and launches communication closure without awaiting it, then rejects. The controller normally interprets this rejection as initialization failure.

After successful start, the first loader is closed, a cancelable progress loader is shown without awaiting its button promise, and worker polling begins. Each nonaborted iteration awaits gts.util.wait(200), sends {reqType:0,reqBody:[49,3,17,3]}, and requires a response body of at least six elements. The masked sixth element determines ERROR_NONE=0 for 2, INIT_FAIL=1 for 3, or COMERROR=2 otherwise.

A check rejection identified by errorCode === gts.ERROR_CODE.NEGATIVE_RESPONSE ('VC000003') with detailCode equal to BUSY_REPEAT_REQUEST ('NRC21') or REQUEST_SEQUENCE_ERROR ('NRC24') repeats the loop, including the next 200-unit wait. Other check errors trigger awaited default-session and communication-close attempts before rejection with result.comResult=COMERROR (2). Successful-length responses also trigger those cleanup attempts before resolving ERROR_NONE (0) or rejecting the other statuses. No independent timer handle, timeout, retry limit or explicit timer cancellation exists locally.

Cancel opens a confirmation dialog and installs a deferred gate that delays controller interpretation of either polling fulfillment or rejection. Yes shows the noncancelable loader, sets controller.isAborted=true, awaits worker abort-flag propagation, and resolves the gate. No reopens the cancelable progress loader and resolves the gate. def is never reset to null after either answer. A later cancellation replaces it with a new deferred.

At the top of a polling iteration, an already-set worker abort flag causes fulfillment with the current errorStatus, initially COMERROR=2, without worker-side session or communication cleanup. The controller ignores that result's status when its own isAborted flag is true, explicitly requests default-session/communication cleanup, closes the loader and emits backToUtilityMenu. Abort is not checked again between an iteration's wait, request and cleanup.

A nonaborted polling fulfillment logs 'This utility is successful', closes the loader and replaces the introductory screen with 'Height Sensor Initialization is completed.' A nonaborted rejection with result.comResult === INIT_FAIL (1) opens the retry warning; COMERROR (2) and all other switch values open inherited showCommErrorDialog. Retry-warning Yes only dismisses/fulfills the dialog handler; it does not automatically repeat Next. No returns to the utility menu.

Exit from the introductory screen asks whether to exit; Yes emits backToUtilityMenu and No does nothing further. Exit from the completion screen emits backToUtilityMenu directly. Controller disposal only disposes currentView and its own event dispatcher: it does not cancel polling, propagate abort, close dialogs, or perform communication cleanup.

In its fulfillment callback, if def === null it returns Promise.resolve(ret); otherwise it waits for controller.def.promise() and then resolves ret. Its catch similarly returns Promise.reject(ret) immediately if def === null, or waits for controller.def.promise() and then rejects ret. The inner catches cover failures arising in their preceding fulfillment callbacks as well as the primary worker operation. Thus a failure during successful-check UI handling can enter the check catch; a failure/rejection escaping that catch can reach the start catch, and an escaping start catch can reach the outer communication-error catch.
The check rejection assumes result.result exists. A differently shaped rejection can throw while reading comResult and flow to the enclosing start catch.

sendStartHeightSensorInitializationRoutine calls gts.util.SendMessageForUtility({reqType:0,reqBody:[0x31,0x01,0x11,0x03]}). Its fulfillment reads response.apiArgs.resBody and rejects if resBody.length < 5, otherwise resolves undefined. Its trailing catch discards all rejection details and rejects undefined.

Local endGeneralComm calls gtsPFApi.endGeneralComm() without arguments; either promise fulfillment or rejection becomes fulfillment.

semantics: Creates new GtsPFApi(), captures cacheData=model.cache.data, sets errorStatus=Rlp01.ERROR_STATUS.COMERROR (2), isloopContinueStatus=true, isNegativeRes=false and resdetailCode=0. param is unused.

while(isloopContinueStatus), try: if(cacheData.isAborted) return createReturnValue(); await gts.util.wait(200); await sendCheckHeightSensorInitializationRoutine(); await transitDefaultSession(); await endGeneralComm(); set isloopContinueStatus=false; if(errorStatus === ERROR_NONE (0)) return createReturnValue(); else return createRejectValue().

sendCheckHeightSensorInitializationRoutine sends {reqType:0,reqBody:[0x31,0x03,0x11,0x03]}. Read response.apiArgs.resBody; if resBody.length < 6, reject undefined. Otherwise if ((resBody[5] & 0xFF) === 0x02), assign ERROR_NONE (0); else if ((resBody[5] & 0xFF) === 0x03), assign INIT_FAIL (1); else assign COMERROR (2). Then resolve undefined.

The send helper's trailing catch(response) assigns isNegativeRes=response?.errorCode === gts.ERROR_CODE.NEGATIVE_RESPONSE ('VC000003') and resdetailCode=response?.detailCode, then rejects undefined. Thus a short-body rejection sets isNegativeRes=false and resdetailCode=undefined. These fields are not reset on later successful responses.

Loop catch(error): if(isNegativeRes && (resdetailCode === gts.DETAIL_CODE.BUSY_REPEAT_REQUEST ('NRC21') || resdetailCode === gts.DETAIL_CODE.REQUEST_SEQUENCE_ERROR ('NRC24'))), set isloopContinueStatus=true and continue. Otherwise await transitDefaultSession(); await endGeneralComm(); set isloopContinueStatus=false; set errorStatus=COMERROR (2); return createRejectValue().
transitDefaultSession calls gtsPFApi.transitSession({modeId:1}) and swallows promise rejection; endGeneralComm calls gtsPFApi.endGeneralComm() without arguments and swallows promise rejection.

createReturnValue resolves {result:{comResult:errorStatus}}; createRejectValue rejects {result:{comResult:errorStatus}}. The returns of rejecting promises are not awaited inside the try, so ordinary INIT_FAIL/COMERROR result rejection does not itself enter the loop catch.
branches: Abort at iteration entry resolves the current status without cleanup; usually that status is the initial COMERROR (2).
Negative-response BUSY_REPEAT_REQUEST ('NRC21') and REQUEST_SEQUENCE_ERROR ('NRC24') retry indefinitely, each via another iteration and wait(200), unless an entry-time abort is observed.
A long-enough response with any sixth masked byte other than 2 or 3 is a terminal COMERROR, not another polling iteration.
No prefix validation, attempt cap, total deadline, explicit timer identifier or clear operation.
Abort during wait/request is not checked until another iteration, if any. A response may finish and close communication before controller abort interpretation.
Unexpected errors outside the send helper can be classified using its previously stored negative-response flags; no normalization is added.
methods.effects_and_cleanup: Normal terminal responses await default-session and communication-close attempts. Nonretry errors do the same then reject COMERROR. Retry and early-abort paths do not do that worker cleanup. No finally.

business_sequence: This unit implements the Signal Check utility. Its instruction screen says it checks whether the Tire Pressure Monitor is operating normally, displays <Attention>, and directs the operator to the repair manual for the detailed signal-check process. The two selectable checks are Transmitter and 2nd Antenna. No ECU behavior beyond the explicit requests, response tests, and resource interpretations below is inferred.

Controller construction initializes all navigation, support, status, and dialog flags. init constructs the local model, view factory, and dialog factory; logs the title Signal Check; displays the empty S_TPW-16-004 view; opens the Please wait. dialog; initializes the worker cache using commonInfo.getCurrentEcuId(); starts communication; discovers supported check types and wheel count; stops communication with defaultSession=true and checkFailure=true; closes the wait dialog; and displays the introductory screen. initTpw16's result field is not checked by the controller.

Communication startup requests startGeneralComm with the cached ECU/bus identifiers, sets repReqRetryMax to 0 while explicitly swallowing rejection of that setting, then requests sessions 0x01 and 0x03 in sequence. Only resultInfo.result === 0 is accepted for startGeneralComm and both startup session transitions. Startup failure becomes {result:false}. Support discovery uses the exact ordered byte requests and bit predicates in the worker contract; individual transmitter and antenna detail failures are tolerated, but neither check being supported makes the overall support result false.

The selection screen disables Transmitter unless counterA === 1 and 2nd Antenna unless counterB === 1. Both radios initially have initValue:false and Next is disabled. A checked radio's change event records its value in the view factory and enables Next. There is no additional controller-side admission validation: Next reads evt.args[1][0].value directly, logs the selected label, opens Please wait., starts communication again, initializes the chosen test flag, closes Please wait., and opens the live result screen.

The live result screen initially shows Incomplete rows. Transmitter shows Transmitter Data ID1 through Transmitter Data ID4 and Transmitter Data ID5 only when wheel === 5; any other view-factory item shows 2nd Antenna. The controller then resets its navigation/status flags and repeatedly awaits confirmTestFlag(item). Each worker call first waits 500 milliseconds, sends the selected read request, and converts the returned byte into status bits. A successful controller iteration replaces status and updates the DOM. There is no success-bit completion condition: Normal, Non-Reception, and Disconnection are displayed values, not loop termination criteria.

Back from the live screen sets back=true and opens Please wait.; it does not cancel the outstanding worker request. After that request resolves, the loop exits before processing its result and calls stopComm(true,true). Successful stop closes the wait dialog and recreates the selection screen, resetting its radio selection.

Exit from the instruction or selection screen opens the Yes/No exit confirmation. Only Yes triggers backToUtilityMenu; No and other resolved button IDs perform no further action. Exit from the live screen sets showDl002=true while the confirmation is pending. A resolved confirmation always clears showDl002; Yes sets exit=true and opens Please wait. The polling loop exits after its current request resolves and eventually calls stopComm(true,false). A failed response while the confirmation is open waits in 100-millisecond increments for the confirmation to resolve; No then produces the ordinary communication-error path, whereas Yes permits the exit path.

After a successful live-screen stop when back is false, the controller logs a table under 'This utility is successful\nDisplayed result on S_TPW-16-003' and emits backToUtilityMenu. This wording is logged even when recorded statuses are Non-Reception, Disconnection, or Incomplete; there is no all-normal predicate. The final report uses the controller's selected item and last stored status, while live rows use the view factory's selected item. Missing/nullish report bits become Incomplete through ?? 2.

Caught initialization failures attempt stopComm(reason.defaultSession,reason.checkFailure), close the tracked wait dialog, show the inherited communication-error dialog, and then navigate to the utility menu. Caught selection-start or live-screen failures use the same cleanup sequence but return to the instruction screen. Cleanup stop results are ignored. Cleanup rejection is not caught again within that cleanup chain. An enclosing selection-start catch can observe rejection of its returned live-screen promise. No method has a finally block, abort mechanism, timer handle, or timer-clear operation. dispose only disposes the current view and controller dispatcher; it does not stop communication, close dialogs, stop polling, or dispose model/view-factory/dialog-factory objects.

All model requests route through GtsWorkerApi.send to six tpw_16.* commands. The separate worker dispatcher supplies param.parameter. Shared framework behavior is available cross-owner at diagnostic_operations.frontend_contracts.MenuShell; gts.common runtime/native owners are likewise separate owners, not missing sources. GtsPFApi and gts.util.SendMessageForUtility retain the exact typed boundaries below; this unit does not redefine their internals. The authoritative constants.js relevant_definitions array is empty; local command/navigation constants and exact numeric request literals are explicitly recorded below. Shared UtilityView event properties are cross-owner references, and undefined event types remain deliverable through the shared dispatcher's coerced property key.

resource_binding.presentation_source: Unit view/dialog methods construct inline DOM or supply typed content/button/table parameters to shared UtilityView/createCommonDialog; no external workflow HTML template path is referenced by these members. Exact inline HTML and options are preserved in source evidence.

business_sequence: The utility presents Data Transmission for Telecom Carrier Cooperation. Its introductory text asks the operator to confirm that the engine/power switch is ON with Engine OFF/Ready OFF and that GTS+ was logged in online. These are instructions, not implemented engine-state checks. The implemented admission check is commonInfo.userInfo.loginMode !== Dcm51.NETWORK_STATUS.ONLINE, numerically !== 1, performed only after retrieving the setting file.

Controller initialization constructs the frontend model, view factory and dialog factory, initializes the model/worker ECU cache, logs the utility title and displays the introductory view. Initialization rejection is passed to inherited onErrorCommon.

Next creates or reuses a buttonless Please wait loader, then sequentially awaits prepSendIccid, readIccid and sendIccid. There is no local busy flag, click suppression, cancellation token, timer or polling loop.

Preparation first requests the user-type setting file with keyList ['sendIccid'], parses its object response and obtains sendIccidRequest_url and id. Only then does the frontend reject a non-ONLINE login with NETWORK_ERROR (1). If admitted, it requests the VIN, pads it to at least 17 characters with spaces, and stores the URL, server ID and VIN in frontend cache.

Reading opens general communication for the selected ECU and bus, transitions to modeId 1 and then modeId 3, reads ICCID using [0x22,0x10,0x18], then IMEI using [0x22,0x10,0x1A]. The worker validates the supplied response-body slices, not an independently implemented ECU/native protocol. ICCID accepts a zero terminator within its first 20 data bytes; IMEI requires 15 digit bytes. Successful reads are followed by default-session restoration and communication closure before caching both strings.

Sending builds a POST/JSON common-runtime web-service request containing JSON.stringify({vin:vin,iccid:iccid,imei:imei}), the configured URL/serverId and makeHeader:1. Success requires parsed commonResult, statusCode exactly 'MIR2000000' and a falsy faultMessage. Other responses and caught failures become SERVER_ERROR (3).

On full success, the controller logs This utility is successful, closes the loader and displays the completed view with only Exit. Exit from that view emits backToUtilityMenu directly. Exit from the introductory view first asks for Yes/No confirmation.

On operation rejection, the controller closes the loader before inspecting e.errorStatus. COM_ERROR (0) and SETTING_FILE_ERROR (4) invoke the inherited communication-error dialog; NETWORK_ERROR (1) and VIN_ERROR (2) show their specific warning and then emit backToUtilityMenu; SERVER_ERROR (3) shows its warning and leaves the current view in place. Unknown errorStatus has no further action. No finally block exists.

Communication cleanup is explicitly sequenced in the frontend model, not in a global dispose path. The worker's end-session and end-communication promise rejection callbacks resolve instead of propagating those API rejections. Controller disposal disposes the current view and its event dispatcher only; it does not stop pending work, close dialogs, dispose the model or unregister the worker.
